akhfash:6-6.t: He said ﴿وَلاَ تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرْ﴾: jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the prohibition. Some read it in the nominative, ﴿وَلاَ تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾, meaning "seeking increase" (مستكثرا), and that is the better of the two meanings. «[Translator's note: the nominative تَسْتَكْثِرُ is the reading of the standard text; the jussive is a variant reading.]»

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهُ كان لآيَاتِنَا عَنِيداً﴾, that is: obstinate (معاندا).

akhfash:33-33.t: And He said ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ﴾; and "دَبَرَ" has the meaning of "أَدْبَرَ" ("to turn away"). They say "قَبَّحَ اللهُ ما قَبَلَ مِنْهُ وما دَبَر" ("may Allah make hideous what came of it and what went"), and they said "عامٌ قَابِلٌ" ("the coming year") and did not say "مُقْبِلٌ".

akhfash:35-36.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّهَا لإِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ﴾ ﴿نَذِيراً لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾: ﴿نَذِيراً﴾ is accusative because it is a khabar (predicate) to ﴿إِحْدَى الكُبَر﴾; ﴿نَذِيراً﴾ is accusative because it is a predicate to a definite noun and the sentence was already complete before it (silence there being acceptable), so it became a ḥāl (circumstantial); and it (the feminine referent) is "the warner" — just as you say "إِنَّهُ لَعَبْدُ اللهِ قَائِماً" ("he is indeed ʿAbdullāh, standing"). And some said: "it is only" "قُمْ نَذِيراً فَأَنْذِر" ("arise as a warner and warn"). «[Translator's note: i.e., they link نَذِيرًا to the command at the opening of the sura, «قُمْ فَأَنْذِرْ» (74:2).]»

akhfash:54-54.t: And He said ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾, that is: the Qur'an is a reminder.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ﴾ the Prophet ﷺ; its underlying form is الْمُتَدَثِّرُ, with the tāʾ assimilated into the dāl, i.e. the one wrapped in his garments when the revelation came down upon him.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿قُمْ فَأَنْذِرْ﴾ make the people of Mecca fear the Fire if they do not believe,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ﴾ magnify [Him] above the associating of partners by the idolaters,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾ from impurity; or shorten them, unlike the Arabs' trailing of their garments out of pride, since impurity might then strike them,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَالرُّجْزَ﴾ the Prophet ﷺ explained it as the idols ﴿فَاهْجُرْ﴾ i.e. persist in shunning it,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَلَا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾ in the nominative, a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. do not give something in order to seek more than it; and this is particular to him ﷺ, because he was commanded with the finest character and the noblest manners;

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَلِرَبِّكَ فَاصْبِرْ﴾ in [keeping] the commands and prohibitions.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ﴾ the trumpet is blown, which is the horn — the second blowing —

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿فَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the time of the blowing ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) for what precedes it, the mubtadaʾ (subject); it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is annexed to something not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin); and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is ﴿يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ﴾; what governs إِذَا is what the clause indicates, i.e. the matter became severe,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ﴾ this indicates that it is easy for the believers, i.e. despite its hardship.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿ذَرْنِي﴾ leave Me ﴿وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ﴾ conjoined to the object, or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) ﴿وَحِيدًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مَنْ, or from its pronoun omitted from خَلَقْتُ, i.e. alone, with neither family nor wealth; he is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī;

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالًا مَمْدُودًا﴾ extensive and continuous, of crops, livestock and trade,

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَبَنِينَ﴾ ten or more ﴿شُهُودًا﴾ who attend gatherings and whose testimony is heard,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَمَهَّدْتُ﴾ I spread out ﴿لَهُ﴾ in livelihood, lifespan and children ﴿تَمْهِيدًا﴾

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يَطْمَعُ أَنْ أَزِيدَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ I will not give him more than that; ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ لِآيَاتِنَا﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿عَنِيدًا﴾ obstinately opposed.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ﴾ I will impose on him ﴿صَعُودًا﴾ a hardship of punishment, or a mountain of fire which he climbs and then falls down from, forever.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ﴾ about what to say regarding the Quran that he had heard from the Prophet ﷺ ﴿وَقَدَّرَ﴾ that in himself.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿فَقُتِلَ﴾ may he be cursed and punished; ﴿كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾ in whatever state his deliberation was;

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿ثُمَّ نَظَرَ﴾ at the faces of his people, or at what he might use to disparage it,

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿ثُمَّ عَبَسَ﴾ contracted and grimaced his face, being frustrated about what to say, ﴿وَبَسَرَ﴾ increased in contracting and grimacing,

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ﴾ from faith ﴿وَاسْتَكْبَرَ﴾ was too proud to follow the Prophet ﷺ,

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَقَالَ﴾ about what he brought: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ﴾ transmitted from sorcerers;

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هَذَا إِلَّا قَوْلُ الْبَشَرِ﴾ as they said: "It is only a human being who teaches him."

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ﴾ I will make him enter ﴿سَقَرَ﴾ Hell.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سَقَرُ﴾ magnifying its import.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿لَا تُبْقِي وَلَا تَذَرُ﴾ any flesh or sinew without destroying it; then it returns as it was.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿عَلَيْهَا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ﴾ angels, its keepers. One of the unbelievers, who was strong and of great might, said: "I will take care of seventeen for you, and you take care of two for me." Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَائِكَةً﴾ i.e. so they cannot be overpowered, as they imagine; ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ﴾ that ﴿إِلَّا فِتْنَةً﴾ a misguidance ﴿لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ in that they say: why are they nineteen? ﴿لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ﴾ that they may be clear about it ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ i.e. the Jews, that the Prophet ﷺ spoke the truth about their being nineteen, which agrees with what is in their scripture; ﴿وَيَزْدَادَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ of the People of the Book ﴿إِيمَانًا﴾ belief, because what the Prophet ﷺ brought agrees with what is in their scripture; ﴿وَلَا يَرْتَابَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ others besides them, concerning the number of the angels; ﴿وَلِيَقُولَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ doubt, in Medina, ﴿وَالْكَافِرُونَ﴾ in Mecca: ﴿مَاذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا﴾ number ﴿مَثَلًا﴾ they called it that because of its strangeness, and it is parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. like the misguiding of the one who rejects this number and the guiding of the one who accepts it ﴿يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ﴾ i.e. the angels, in their strength and their helpers, ﴿إِلَّا هُوَ وَمَا هِيَ﴾ i.e. Saqar ﴿إِلَّا ذِكْرَى لِلْبَشَرِ﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ an opening particle (istiftāḥ) in the sense of أَلَا; ﴿وَالْقَمَرِ﴾

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا﴾ with fatḥa on the dhāl ﴿دَبَرَ﴾ came after the day; in one reading [إِذْ أَدْبَرَ] with sukūn on the dhāl followed by a hamza, i.e. passed away;

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿إِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. Saqar ﴿لَإِحْدَى الْكُبَرِ﴾ the great calamities,

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿نَذِيرًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إِحْدَى; it is masculine because it is in the sense of "the punishment"; ﴿لِلْبَشَرِ﴾

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for الْبَشَرِ ﴿أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ﴾ to good, or to Paradise, through faith, ﴿أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ﴾ to evil, or to the Fire, through unbelief.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ﴾ pledged, held in the Fire for its deeds,

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿إِلَّا أَصْحَابَ الْيَمِينِ﴾ and they are the believers, who are saved from it, being

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ and their state, and they say to them, after the monotheists have been taken out of the Fire:

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَكُنَّا نُكَذِّبُ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾ the resurrection and the recompense,

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿فَمَا تَنْفَعُهُمْ شَفَاعَةُ الشَّافِعِينَ﴾ of the angels, the prophets and the righteous; the meaning is: they have no intercession.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿فَمَا﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ its khabar (predicate), attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted [word] whose pronoun has moved to it; ﴿عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun; the meaning is: what has come over them in their turning away from taking admonition?

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿فَرَّتْ مِنْ قَسْوَرَةٍ﴾ a lion, i.e. fled from it in the most intense flight.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُؤْتَى صُحُفًا مُنَشَّرَةً﴾ i.e. from Allah the Exalted, [commanding them] to follow the Prophet, as they said: "We will not believe in you until you bring down to us a book we can read."

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a deterrent from what they wanted; ﴿بَلْ لَا يَخَافُونَ الْآخِرَةَ﴾ i.e. its punishment.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ an opening particle (istiftāḥ); ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾ an admonition;

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ﴾ read it and took admonition from it.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ هُوَ أَهْلُ التَّقْوَى﴾ [worthy] of being feared ﴿وَأَهْلُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ [worthy] of forgiving whoever fears Him.

daas-irab:1-7.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), and hā is a particle of alerting (tanbīh); and ﴿الْمُدَّثِّرُ﴾ badal (substitute) of أيّ; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿قُمْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿فَأَنْذِرْ﴾ an imperative verb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to قم; the clause قم is also initial, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَرَبَّكَ﴾ a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَكَبِّرْ﴾ the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of an omitted condition, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَثِيابَكَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a fronted mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَطَهِّرْ﴾ parsed like فكبر. ﴿وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تَمْنُنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وَلِرَبِّكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ the i'rab of its like has preceded.

daas-irab:8-10.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿إذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive. ﴿نُقِرَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿فِي النَّاقُورِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿فَذلِكَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; and ﴿يَوْمٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; and ﴿عَسِيرٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition, with no grammatical position; and ﴿عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عسير; and ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ a second adjective of يوم; and ﴿يَسِيرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:11-12.t: ﴿ذَرْنِي﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the first person is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the yāʾ of the first person; and ﴿خَلَقْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَحِيداً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and they stand in the place of the second object; and ﴿مالًا﴾ its first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مَمْدُوداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:13-15.t: ﴿وَبَنِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to مالا; and ﴿شُهُوداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَمَهَّدْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿تَمْهِيداً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿يَطْمَعُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ أَزِيدَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, whose fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ).

daas-irab:16-17.t: ﴿كَلَّا إِنَّهُ﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr), and inna and its noun; and ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿لِآياتِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; and ﴿عَنِيداً﴾ khabar (predicate) of kāna; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ﴾ the sīn of futurity, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent, and the hāʾ is first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿صَعُوداً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-23.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنه, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl). ﴿وَقَدَّرَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فكر; and ﴿فَقُتِلَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; and ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun as ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿قَدَّرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and the verses that follow are conjoined to it, up to verse 23.

daas-irab:24-25.t: ﴿فَقالَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿إِنْ هذا﴾ in is negative, and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿سِحْرٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and ﴿يُؤْثَرُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of سحر; and ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative; and ﴿هذا﴾ the demonstrative as mubtadaʾ; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; and ﴿قَوْلُ الْبَشَرِ﴾ khabar, annexed to البشر; the clause is an emphasis (taʾkīd) of the preceding one.

daas-irab:26-30.t: ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ﴾ the sīn of futurity, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿سَقَرَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is badal (substitute) of سأرهقه. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; and ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ما سَقَرُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك; and ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿تُبْقِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; and ﴿لا تَذَرُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿لَوَّاحَةٌ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; and ﴿لِلْبَشَرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; the clause is a second ḥāl; and ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ a fronted khabar; and ﴿تِسْعَةَ﴾ part of a number, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a postponed mubtadaʾ; and ﴿عَشَرَ﴾ part of a number, indeclinable on fatḥa, with no grammatical position. The clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿ما﴾ negative; and ﴿جَعَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿أَصْحابَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to ﴿النَّارِ﴾; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿مَلائِكَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَما جَعَلْنا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿عِدَّتَهُمْ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; and ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being «a cause of trial» (سبب فتنة); and ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; and ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). And ﴿لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to the second جعلنا; and ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil; and ﴿أُوتُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيَزْدادَ﴾ conjoined to ليستيقن; and ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil; and ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين; and ﴿إِيماناً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَلا يَرْتابَ الَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿لا﴾ negative, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿أُوتُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; and ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ conjoined to الذين; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلِيَقُولَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied an after the lām of purpose; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are conjoined to «ليستيقن..»; and ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil; and ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿مَرَضٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿وَالْكافِرُونَ﴾ conjoined to الذين; and ﴿ماذا﴾ an interrogative noun, a fronted mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿أَرادَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and ﴿بِهذا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿مَثَلًا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). And ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and ﴿يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle and mā is negative; and ﴿يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, annexed to ربك; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; and ﴿هُوَ﴾ fāʿil of يعلم; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive and mā is negative; and ﴿هِيَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; and ﴿ذِكْرى لِلْبَشَرِ﴾ khabar, to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:32-37.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿وَالْقَمَرِ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition, and a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of oath. ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time; and ﴿أَدْبَرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَالصُّبْحِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time; and ﴿أَسْفَرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation; and ﴿إِنَّها لَإِحْدَى﴾ inna and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and ﴿إحدى الْكُبَرِ﴾ khabar (predicate) of inna, annexed to الكبر; the nominal clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. And ﴿نَذِيراً﴾ tamyīz (specification); and ﴿لِلْبَشَرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نذيرا; and ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, badal (substitute) of His words للبشر; and ﴿شاءَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); and ﴿أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿يَتَأَخَّرَ﴾ conjoined to يتقدم.

daas-irab:38-42.t: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to نفس; and ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كسبت; and ﴿كَسَبَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿رَهِينَةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; and ﴿أَصْحابَ الْيَمِينِ﴾ excepted (mustathnā) by illā, annexed to اليمين; and ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what precedes them; and ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ; and ﴿سَلَكَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; and ﴿فِي سَقَرَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the nominal clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl li-qawl maḥdhūf).

daas-irab:43-47.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿لَمْ نَكُ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn on the nūn, which is dropped for lightness, and its noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of نك; the verbal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلَمْ نَكُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding one; and ﴿نُطْعِمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿الْمِسْكِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «نطعم..» is the khabar of نك. ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾ a defective past verb, and nā is its noun; and ﴿نَخُوضُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of كنا, and the clause «كنا..» is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place, annexed to ﴿الْخائِضِينَ﴾. ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾ conjoined to the preceding one; and ﴿نُكَذِّبُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of كنا; and ﴿بِيَوْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الدِّينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit and a preposition; and ﴿أَتانَا﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿الْيَقِينُ﴾ its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by ḥattā, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to نكذب.

daas-irab:48-51.t: ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; and ﴿ما﴾ negative; and ﴿تَنْفَعُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿شَفاعَةُ﴾ fāʿil (agent), annexed to ﴿الشَّافِعِينَ﴾; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ ḥāl; and ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ﴾ kaʾanna, its noun and its predicate. ﴿مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَرَّتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مِنْ قَسْوَرَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is a second adjective of حمر.

daas-irab:52-53.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb); and ﴿يُرِيدُ كُلُّ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), annexed to ﴿امْرِئٍ﴾; and ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of امرئ; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿أَنْ يُؤْتى﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿صُحُفاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿مُنَشَّرَةً﴾ an adjective of صحفا; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr); and ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression; and ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿يَخافُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; and ﴿الْآخِرَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:54-56.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ an emphasis (tawkīd) of what precedes it; and ﴿إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾ and its noun and its predicate [Translator's note: so in the source; «inna» is evidently dropped: inna, its noun and its predicate]; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; and ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; and ﴿من﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿شاءَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); and ﴿ذَكَرَهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ negative; and ﴿يَذْكُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; and ﴿أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is accusative by exception; and ﴿هُوَ أَهْلُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, annexed to ﴿التَّقْوى﴾; the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position; and ﴿أَهْلُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:1-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمُدَّثِّرُ): the one wearing the دثار, which is what is worn over the شعار, i.e. the garment next to the body. Its origin is المتدثر; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl, as already mentioned at المزمل. It means the one wrapped in his garments when the revelation came down upon him. It is narrated from Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I was on Mount Ḥirāʾ and I was called: O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of Allah. I looked to my right and my left and saw nothing; then I looked above me and there he was, seated on a throne between heaven and earth" — meaning the angel who had called him — "so I was terrified and returned to Khadīja and said: Cover me, cover me! Then Jibrīl came down and said: يا أيها المدثر."
(الرُّجْزَ): with kasra on the rāʾ, which is the reading of the majority; Ḥafṣ, Mujāhid, al-Sulamī and others read it with ḍamma. It has been said that both have one meaning, the idols and graven images being intended. It has also been said: the kasra is for denoting shameful deeds and depravity, and the ḍamma for the two idols Isāf and Nāʾila. Al-Ḥasan said: every act of disobedience. The meaning of the command then is: be firm and persist in shunning it, because he ﷺ was already free of it. Al-Nakhaʿī said: sin. Al-Qutabī said: punishment, i.e. shun what leads to it. Al-Zamakhsharī adopted this and said:
«الرجز, with kasra and ḍamma, is punishment, and its meaning is: shun what leads to it, namely idol-worship and other sins. The meaning is steadfastness in shunning it, because he was already free of it». In al-Qāmūs: «الرجز, with kasra and ḍamma: filth, idol-worship and polytheism». The zāy is changed from sīn (i.e. رجس); the Arabs alternate between the two, and the meaning is one.
(النَّاقُورِ): النقر is sound. The poet said:
أخفضه بالنقر لما علوته ... ويرفع طرفا غير خاف غضيض
(I calm him with a click of the tongue when I mount him, and he raises an eye that is neither hidden nor lowered.)
الناقور is of the pattern فاعول from it, like الجاسوس taken from التجسس. What is meant here is the Trumpet (الصور), which is the horn.
(وَمَهَّدْتُ لَهُ تَمْهِيداً): التمهيد originally means levelling and preparing, and it is used figuratively for the spreading out of wealth and standing. In al-Kashshāf: «I spread out for him broad standing and leadership among his people, and so completed upon him My two favours, wealth and standing».
(عَبَسَ): عبس يعبس عبسا وعبوسا: he knitted his face (frowned); its verb class is that of جلس. العبس is the dung and urine that dries on the tails of camels.
(بَسَرَ): بسر يبسر بسرا وبسورا: when he contracts what is between his eyes in dislike of something and his face darkens because of it; its verb class is that of دخل. One says وجه باسر, i.e. contracted and dark. Al-Rāghib said: «البسر is hastening something before its time, as in بسر الرجل حاجته: he sought it out of its time; and ماء بسر: water taken from a pool before it has settled; and from it the unripe date is called بسر. His saying, the Exalted: (عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ), means he displayed frowning before its time and occasion. If it is said: in His saying, the Exalted, «ووجوه يومئذ باسرة» they do not do that before the time, whereas you said that this word is for what happens before its time — it is replied: by that is indicated their state before reaching the Fire; the word البسر was singled out [Translator's note: the source has فحص, evidently a misprint for فخصّ] to point out that this, along with what befalls them of it, runs the course of what is imposed and of what is done before its time; and His saying تظن أن يفعل بها فاقرة indicates that».
(سَقَرَ): one of the names of Hell; it is a diptote because of being a proper name and feminine.
(لَوَّاحَةٌ): scorching the outer skin. It is an intensive form, and it has two meanings. The first is from لاح يلوح, i.e. it appeared — meaning that it appears to people. The second, which is preferable, is that it is from لوّحه, i.e. he altered it and blackened it. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «لواحة is from لوح الهجير (the scorching of the midday heat). He said:
تقول ما لاحك يا مسافر ... يا ابنة عمي لاحني الهواجر
(She says: What has scorched you, O traveller? O my cousin, the midday heats have scorched me.)
It is said: it scorches the skin one scorching and leaves it blacker than the night; and البشر [here] is the outer surface of the skins».

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ قُمْ فَأَنْذِرْ وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ): the i'rab of يا أيها المدثر was given at يا أيها المزمل. قم is an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت; فأنذر is conjoined to قم. Al-Zajjāj said: «The fāʾ in فكبر entered with the sense of requital (jazāʾ), as it entered in فأنذر. Ibn Jinnī said: it is like your saying زيدا فاضرب, i.e. زيدا اضرب, so the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida)». The wāw is a conjunction; ربك is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The fāʾ links to an implied condition required by the context, as though it were said: "and whatever happens, do not abandon magnifying Him". Similar is your saying زيدا فاضربه; the grammarians said its implied form is "be alert, and strike Zayd", so the fāʾ is in answer to the command, either because it carries the sense of a condition or because the condition after it is omitted, according to the disagreement on this among them. كبر is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being أنت.
(وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ): the wāw is a conjunction; ثيابك is a fronted object; the fāʾ was discussed just above; طهر is an imperative verb.
(وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ): likewise conjoined to what precedes.
(وَلا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تمنن is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; تستكثر is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), whose agent is latent, its implied form being أنت, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "and do not give seeking more". It was also read in the jussive, either as the answer to the prohibition or as a badal (substitute) of تمنن. The implied meaning on taking it as the answer to the prohibition is: if you do not remind people of your favour for your deed or your gift, you will gain more reward, because it is kept safe from being nullified by reminding of favours, in the manner of His saying, the Exalted: «لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى». The basis for the substitution is that it is like His saying, the Exalted: «ومن يفعل ذلك يلق أثاما يضاعف له العذاب», in the reading of the one who made it jussive as a substitute of يلق, and like the poet's saying:
متى تأتنا تلمم بنا في ديارنا ... تجد حطبا جزلا ونارا تأججا
(Whenever you come to us, stopping by us in our dwellings, you will find thick firewood and a fire ablaze.)
(وَلِرَبِّكَ فَاصْبِرْ): the wāw is a conjunction; لربك is attached (mutaʿalliq) to اصبر.
(فَإِذا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ): the fāʾ is for causation and giving the reason, as though He said: be patient with their harm, for before them is a hard day on which they will meet the consequence of their harm and you will meet the outcome of your patience. إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time; it is attached to what is indicated by the demonstrative in His saying فذلك, since it points to the blowing. It may also be attached to what عسير indicates, though عسير itself does not govern it, because an adjective does not govern what precedes it; the implied form is "the matter becomes severe and hard". نقر is a passive past verb, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being هو, i.e. Isrāfīl [Translator's note: so in the source; the deputy agent is more usually taken to be the Trumpet, i.e. the blowing is done "in" it].
The clause is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and في الناقور is attached to نقر.
(فَذلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ): the fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the demonstrative pointing to the time of the blowing; يومئذ is a substitute of ذلك, made indeclinable (mabnī) because it is annexed to a non-declinable word, namely إذ, and the tanwīn compensates for a clause, i.e. "the day when the Trumpet is blown". يوم is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ and عسير is a naʿt (adjective).
(عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ): على الكافرين is attached to عسير, and غير يسير is a second adjective of يوم. Al-Zamakhsharī has a fine explanation; he said: «If you ask: what is the benefit of His saying غير يسير when عسير suffices? I say: when He said على الكافرين, restricting the hardship to them, He said غير يسير to announce that it will not be for them as it will be for the believers — easy and pleasant — so as to combine the threat to the disbelievers and the increase of their rage with good tidings and consolation for the believers. It may also be intended that it is hard and there is no hope that it will turn easy, as there is hope that hard matters of this world become easy».
(ذَرْنِي وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وَحِيداً): ذرني is an imperative verb; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya); the agent is latent, its implied form being أنت; the yāʾ is the object. As for ومن: the wāw is of accompaniment and من is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); the wāw may also be a conjunction, with من conjoined to the object in ذرني. The clause خلقت is the ṣila (relative clause) and the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. خلقته. وحيدا is a ḥāl from the omitted referring pronoun, or a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun in ذرني, or from the tāʾ in خلقت, i.e. "I created him alone, no one sharing with Me in creating him, so I will destroy him and need no helper". It has been said that the first is preferable, because the one meant is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī, father of Khālid ibn al-Walīd, since he used to claim that he was unique among his people in his leadership, his wealth and his worldly pre-eminence. There is nothing in that which requires that his claim be true, because this was a byname he was famous by, and a person may be given a byname with a quality he does not possess. It has also been said that it is general.
(وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مالًا مَمْدُوداً): conjoined to what precedes; له is attached to an omitted element which is the second object; مالا is the first object, and ممدودا is an adjective. It is said to be the crops, livestock and trade al-Walīd had in Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.
(وَبَنِينَ شُهُوداً): conjoined to مال. It is said that al-Walīd had ten male children, or seven, namely al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd, Khālid, ʿUmāra, Hishām, al-ʿĀṣ, Qays and ʿAbd Shams. Three of them became Muslims: Khālid, Hishām and ʿUmāra. It is reported from Ibn Ḥajar in al-Iṣāba that ʿUmāra died a disbeliever, and he mentioned al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd in his place, so they are Khālid, Hishām and al-Walīd. شهودا is an adjective of بنين [Translator's note: the source has «لنبين», a misprint for لبنين], plural of شاهد meaning "present"; they attend councils and gatherings with their father.
(وَمَهَّدْتُ لَهُ تَمْهِيداً): conjoined to what precedes; له is attached to مهدت, and تمهيدا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(ثُمَّ يَطْمَعُ أَنْ أَزِيدَ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay, and in it there is a sense of finding it far-fetched and reprehensible that he should be greedy, covetous and eager for more wealth and favour. يطمع is an imperfect verb, nominative, conjoined to جعلت and مهدت, whose agent is latent, its implied form being هو. أن and what lies within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, attached to يطمع, i.e. he covets increase over what was mentioned of wealth, sons and smoothing of the way.
(كَلَّا إِنَّهُ كانَ لِآياتِنا عَنِيداً): كلا is a deterrent and rebuke to him, to cut off his hope, greed and eagerness. إنّ and what follows it is a clause giving the reason for the deterrent, because obstinately opposing the signs of the Benefactor despite their clarity, and being ungrateful for them despite their prevalence, are among the things that destroy the soul and bring about deprivation. إنّ and its noun; the clause كان is its khabar; the noun of كان is latent, its implied form being هو; لآياتنا is attached to عنيدا, and عنيدا is its khabar. العنيد is the one who denies, turns away and avoids the truth and guidance; its plural is عُنُد.
(سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً): the sīn is a particle of the future; أرهقه is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; صعودا is a second direct object because أرهقه carries the sense of أكلفه ("I will impose on him"). الصعود in the language is a difficult mountain ascent. If أرهقه is not taken to carry the sense of أكلفه, then صعودا is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "I will distress him with hardship and difficulty".
(إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ): giving the reason for his deserving this threat just mentioned. إنّ and its noun; the clause فكر is the khabar, and قدر is conjoined to فكر. It is narrated that al-Walīd argued with Abū Jahl and a group of Quraysh about the Qurʾān and said: "It has a sweetness; its lower part is abundant [Translator's note: the source has لمفرقه; the usual wording of the report is لمغدق], its branch is fruitful, it crushes what is beneath it, and it rises high and is not risen above", and words like this. They opposed him and said: "It is poetry." He said: "By Allah, it is not poetry; we know poetry, its hazaj and its basīṭ." They said: "Then he is a soothsayer." He said: "By Allah, he is not a soothsayer; we have seen the soothsayers." They said: "He is mad." He said: "By Allah, he is not mad; we have seen the madman and his choking fits." They said: "It is magic." He said: "As for this, it is likely that it is magic", and he would say his own sayings. Other versions are narrated that do not go beyond these meanings, for which one may refer to the longer works.
(فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; قتل is a passive past verb, and its deputy agent is latent, its implied form being هو. Its meaning is "he was cursed"; it has also been said: "he was overcome and subdued". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
وما ذرفت عيناك إلا لتضربي ... بسهميك في أعشار قلب مقتل
(Your eyes shed tears only so that you might strike with your two arrows into the fragments of a heart subdued.)
i.e. humbled and subdued by love. If its meaning is "he was cursed", the clause is one of imprecation (duʿāʾiyya); if its meaning is "he was overcome and subdued", the clause is conjoined to what precedes. كيف is an interrogative noun, accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in قدر; the purpose of the question is wonder at his deliberation, rebuke and mockery of him.
(ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence and delay; it was brought to indicate that this clause is more forceful than the first, so it is for difference in rank. It emphasizes its counterpart that came before, so the repetition is for emphasis.
(ثُمَّ نَظَرَ): ثم is also a conjunction for sequence with delay, i.e. he looked into people's faces, angered by what they had said about him, namely that he had changed religion and inclined to Muhammad.
(ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ): also conjoined, i.e. then he knitted his face, then looked askance and narrowed his eyes in arrogance.
(ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ): also conjoined, i.e. he turned his back on faith and was too proud to follow the Prophet; so it is a conjunction of equivalent meaning.
فقال: (إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is negative; هذا is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; سحر is the khabar, and the clause يؤثر is an adjective of سحر, i.e. handed down from the magicians.
(إِنْ هذا إِلَّا قَوْلُ الْبَشَرِ): this clause is an emphasis of the previous clause, i.e. picked up from people's sayings.
(سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ): the sīn is a particle of the future; أصليه is an imperfect verb, a latent agent, its implied form being أنا, and a first direct object; سقر is a second direct object. The whole clause is a substitute of His saying سأرهقه صعودا.
(وَما أَدْراكَ ما سَقَرُ): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; أدراك is a past verb, a latent agent, its implied form being هو, and a first direct object; the clause is the khabar of ما, i.e. "what has made you know?". ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and سقر is its khabar; the clause fills the place of the second object of أدراك, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing by the interrogative. Its like was given in al-Ḥāqqa.
(لا تُبْقِي وَلا تَذَرُ): the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and what governs it is the sense of making its matter terrifying and great, because the question in ما سقر is for magnification; the meaning is: regard Saqar as tremendous in this state. لا is negative; تبقي is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being هي; تذر is conjoined to تبقي. The object of تبقي and تذر is omitted, i.e. it does not spare what is thrown into it, nor does it leave it, but destroys it. You may also make it a resumptive clause.
(لَوَّاحَةٌ لِلْبَشَرِ): لواحة is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; للبشر is attached to لواحة, and the clause is a second ḥāl. لواحةً was also read in the accusative as a ḥāl: it has been said to be a ḥāl from سقر, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in لا تبقي, or from the pronoun in لا تذر. Al-Zamakhsharī chose to make it accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) for the sake of terrifying.
(عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ): the clause is a third ḥāl, or resumptive, as was said at لواحة للبشر. عليها is a fronted khabar, and تسعة عشر are two numeral parts, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ. More on the meaning of this number will come in the Rhetoric section.
(وَما جَعَلْنا أَصْحابَ النَّارِ إِلَّا مَلائِكَةً): the wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to answer Abū al-Ashadd [Translator's note: the source has «أبي الأشد به كلدة», apparently a corruption of «أبي الأشدّ بن كلدة»] ibn Kalada ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī. Ibn ʿAbbās said: When this verse came down, «عليها تسعة عشر», Abū Jahl said to Quraysh:
"May your mothers be bereaved of you! Muhammad reports that the keepers of the Fire are nineteen, while you are the brave ones; is every ten of you unable to seize one of them?" Abū al-Ashadd said: "I will deal with seventeen of them for you: ten on my back and seven on my belly, and you deal with two for me." So it came down. ما is negative; جعلنا is a past verb and its agent; أصحاب النار is the first direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction, and ملائكة is the second direct object, i.e. We did not make them men of your kind whom you could overpower; We made them only angels who cannot be withstood.
(وَما جَعَلْنا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; جعلنا is a past verb and its agent; عدتهم is a direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; فتنة is a second direct object with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "a cause of trial". It is not a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), as might be imagined. للذين is attached to فتنة, and the clause كفروا is the ṣila.
(لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ وَيَزْدادَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِيماناً): the lām is the lām of reason (taʿlīl); يستيقن is an imperfect verb, accusative by أن optionally concealed after the lām of reason. It is attached to the second جعلنا, not to فتنة, because the trial is not caused by the certainty; rather what is caused is making the number a cause of trial for those given the Book [Translator's note: so in the source; the trial in the verse is for «الذين كفروا»]. It has also been said that ليستيقن is attached to a concealed verb, i.e. "We did that so that … may be certain". الذين is the agent; the clause أوتوا الكتاب is the ṣila; الكتاب is the second object of أوتوا, because the wāw is the deputy agent of أوتوا. يزداد is conjoined to ليستيقن; الذين is the agent; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila, and إيمانا is a second direct object.
(وَلا يَرْتابَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; يرتاب الذين is an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause أوتوا الكتاب is the ṣila, and المؤمنون is conjoined to الذين.
(وَلِيَقُولَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ وَالْكافِرُونَ ماذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِهذا مَثَلًا): conjoined to what precedes. The lām is the lām of reason; الذين is the agent; في قلوبهم is a fronted khabar and مرض a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ماذا is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted object of أراد; بهذا is attached to أراد; مثلا is a ḥāl from هذا, i.e. in the state of resembling a parable. You may also make ما an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ and ذا a relative noun as its khabar, with أراد الله as the ṣila of the relative. The clause ماذا أراد … is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(كَذلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ): كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar: He sends astray with a sending-astray like that. الله is the agent of يضل and من its object; the clause يشاء is the ṣila and the referring pronoun is omitted. ويهدي من يشاء is conjoined to the previous clause.
(وَما يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ): the clause is resumptive.
(وَما هِيَ إِلَّا ذِكْرى لِلْبَشَرِ): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; هي is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the pronoun referring to Saqar; إلا is a particle of restriction; ذكرى is the khabar, and للبشر is attached to ذكرى.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying, the Exalted, (عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ) there is the device of ibhām (deliberate ambiguity). We alluded to it earlier in this book, and we repeat it here in more detail because of the importance of this verse and how much the scholars of rhetoric and the exegetes have delved into it. We say: ibhām is one of the devices of rhetoric. It is that the speaker says something that bears two different meanings, neither of which is distinguished from the other. The difference between it and faulty homonymy (al-ishtirāk) is that homonymy occurs only in a single word with two senses where it is not known which the speaker intended, whereas ibhām occurs only in composed, meaningful sentences, and it is specific to genres such as praise, satire, reproach, apology, boasting, elegy, love-poetry and so on. There is another kind of it which occurs for one of two purposes: either to test the excellence of the mind or to test the strength and weakness of faith. This verse before us is of this kind, i.e. a test of the strength and weakness of faith, for the meaning of (عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ) is ambiguous in the extreme, and someone may ask: what is the subtle point in mentioning this number?
It should not be said that this question falls away because it would arise for any number assumed — so that if it were said "over it are fifteen" or "eleven" or "twenty" or other than that, the question would arise against it, and whatever is of this kind falls away — because we say: this applies to what comes from a created being, whose report may fail and who is not protected from lying. As for the Creator, Glorified is He, whose report does not fail and who, when He reports something, it is as He reported, when He reports a number it may not be said of it "had He said another, the question would arise", because it is the truth that is actual and beyond doubt. That being so, someone may ask: what is the wisdom in making the angels of punishment of this number?
So the question is valid and deserves an answer, so that this ambiguity on the surface of the speech may be removed. We shall now give a summary of what the great authorities said in explaining this ambiguity, and after that give an opinion we have preferred over the others, so that there may be in this something to engage the mind and stir talents — though we have not included what we saw as unworthy of attention.
As for the Imām Fakhr al-Dīn ibn al-Khaṭīb [al-Rāzī], he held a view with much soundness and judiciousness. He said: «Since the responsible person (mukallaf) consists of outward senses and inward senses, which are ten, and natures and five faculties, namely the digestive, the nutritive, the retentive and the propulsive [Translator's note: only four are listed in the source], and since these things are what call to occupation with worldly pleasures and bestial desires and to warding off bodily harms, away from occupation with what brings near to the Gardens and keeps far from the Fires, and since the number of these things is nineteen, the angels charged with punishing man were made according to this number, so that facing each of these things there is an angel charged with exacting what is due upon that thing, which is one of the causes that prevent good».
This is what al-Rāzī mentioned, and despite its merit and value it is not free of strain. As for al-Karkhī, he abridged what al-Rāzī mentioned and added to it from another angle, saying: «This number was singled out for mention because it agrees with the number of the causes of corruption of the human soul, which are the human and the natural faculties. The human faculties are twelve: the five outward, the five inward, desire and anger. The natural faculties are seven: the attractive, the retentive, the digestive, the expulsive, the nutritive [Translator's note: the source has العادية, evidently a misprint for الغاذية], the growth faculty and the generative. The total is nineteen».
As for the earlier scholars, foremost among them al-Zamakhsharī, they drew a fine rhetorical inference. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The nature of this number, falling one short of the decade of twenty, is that whoever does not believe in Allah and His wisdom will be put to trial by it, objecting and mocking and not submitting as the believer submits even if the reason for the wisdom is hidden from him. It is as though it were said: We have made their number a number whose nature is that people are tried by it, for the sake of the believer's certainty and the disbeliever's perplexity; and the certainty of the People of the Book, because their number is nineteen in the two Books, so when they hear its like in the Qurʾān they are certain it is sent down from Allah; and the believers' increase in faith, by their affirming that as they affirmed all else that was sent down, and because of what they saw of the People of the Book embracing Islam». This, despite its merit, is not free of objection.
As for al-Qurṭubī, he did not go beyond the limits of transmitted report and did not resort to independent reasoning. He said after a long discussion: «I say: what is correct, if Allah wills, is that these nineteen are the chiefs and leaders; as for their total, words fall short of it, as the Exalted said: (وَما يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ)».
As for Abū Ḥayyān, he went on at length and hummed about, now leaping up, now swooping low. Among his words that we select: «عليها تسعة عشر: the tamyīz (specification) is omitted, and what comes first to mind is that it is "angel". Do you not see how the Arabs, who are the eloquent, understood from it that "angel" is meant when they heard that?» He cited the report we have given and then said: «It has also been said that the omitted tamyīz is "a class of angels", and it has been said "a leader". The meaning of عليها is that they are in charge of it, and to them the zabāniya (guards) of it are gathered. What appears from the number, from the verse after that and from the ḥadīth is that these are the leaders». This is almost exactly what al-Qurṭubī said.
As for the opinion of al-Rāzī and al-Karkhī, it is not free of a flaw, given the arbitrariness and strain in it, as you see. The flaw is that it would require every human being to have this number of angels, and it would then not be the total number of the angels of Hell and of all the punished it contains.
As for the technical answer that resolves the ambiguity in a way nearer to logic, more convincing and more in keeping with the eloquence of the Noble Qurʾān, it is to say: there is no doubt that the people of the Fire exceed the people of the Garden many times over, since the believers of every nation are a tenth of a tenth of its disbelievers. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has reported of the Garden that its breadth is the heavens and the earth — so what do you think of its length, when the length of anything is, by accepted custom, greater than the breadth? Its people, accordingly, cannot be counted by number nor confined by limit. And it has become clear that the people of the Fire are many times their number, so they are nearer to exceeding all limit in number. The least that can be supposed of the angels charged with punishing them is that their number matches theirs, so that facing every one punished there is one who punishes; and this is a number without end, nor end to its quantity. So when the Real wished to report the number of these angels, He turned away from mentioning their number, which is known to Him even if it exceeds all end in relation to us — lest the speech, by the multitude of words and length of sections, leave the bounds of eloquence — to an allusion from which it is understood that the number of these angels is a number of unending rank. So He, Glorified is He, confined Himself to mentioning the last rank of the units of number and the first rank of the tens. For the ranks of number are four: units, tens, hundreds and thousands. Their foundations are the units and the first of its ranks [Translator's note: the wording here appears disturbed in the source]. The end of the rank of units is nine, which consists of repeating the one nine times; then one moves to mentioning ten, which is the first rank of the tens, and then repeats it as one repeated the one, from twenty to ninety, as was done in the first rank; then one moves to the rank of thousands and repeats it as the one is repeated, with the words of the units, and so on without end. When the rank of thousands ends, one returns to the rank of tens and says "ten thousand", up to what has no end, adding nothing more than to annex to "thousand" the words of the units and tens, thus returning to the foundations of numbers. This shows that the foundations of all numbers, which are endless, are the units, which are nine, and the first of the tens, which is ten. So confining the mention to these two, for the Arabs who coined these names, points to numbers without end. He dispensed with mentioning the two words "hundred" and "thousand" because of the model in the speech to be followed and the root by which the branch is measured; the two words, i.e. hundred and thousand, are known to the one addressed, and the method of repetition has been made clear.
2- In His saying «وربك فكبر» there is a curious device which the later writers invented and handled badly, because it only comes out well rarely, while forcing it leads to its degradation. The scholars of badīʿ (embellishment) gave it the name «ما لا يستحيل بالانعكاس» ("what does not change when reversed"); some called it «القلب» ("inversion") and others «المقلوب المستوي» ("the even inversion"), i.e. the palindrome. It is that the words are such that if you reverse them and begin from the last letter to the first, the result is these very words. It may occur in verse and in prose. In verse there is the saying of al-Qāḍī al-Arrajānī:
مودته تدوم لكل هول ... وهل كلّ مودته تدوم
(His affection endures through every terror — and does every one's affection endure?)
It may occur in half a verse, as in the saying of the poet:
ولما تبدى لنا وجهه ... أرانا الإله هلالا أنارا
(When his face appeared to us, God showed us a crescent that shone.)
The evidence is in the second hemistich. In prose, Allah the Exalted said: (كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ), (رَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ). It is related of al-ʿImād al-Kātib that he met al-Qāḍī al-Fāḍil one day while he was riding a horse and said to him: «سر فلا كبا بك الفرس» [Translator's note: the source has «ركبا», but the palindrome requires «كبا»] ("Go on, and may the horse not stumble with you"), and al-Qāḍī replied: «دام علا العماد» ("May al-ʿImād's eminence endure"). All of this is palatable and free of strain, so it came out charming and flowing within the bounds of natural expression. As for what they forced, we have turned away from it because it has no connection whatever to eloquence.
3- In His saying, the Exalted, «وثيابك فطهر»: if the actual clothes worn on the body are meant, the speech runs on its literal sense and there is no rhetorical device in it, since the purity of clothes is a condition for the validity of prayer and it is ugly for a believer's clothes to be impure. If the heart is meant, the speech is a kināya (metonymy), in the manner of Imruʾ al-Qays's saying:
وإن تك قد ساءتك مني خليقة ... فسلي ثيابي من ثيابك تنسلي
(If some trait of mine has displeased you, then draw my garments out from yours and they will come away.)
i.e. my heart from your heart. It has also been said that the garments are a kināya for the self. ʿAntara said:
فشككت بالرمح الطويل ثيابه ... ليس الكريم عن القنا بمحرم
(I pierced his garments with the long spear; the noble man is not immune to the lances.)
It has also been said that it is a kināya for the body. Laylā said, mentioning camels:
رموها بأثواب خفاف فلا نرى ... لها شبها إلا النعام المنضرا
(They cast upon them light garments, and we see no likeness to them but ostriches startled away.)
i.e. they mounted them, casting themselves upon them.

dervis-irab:32-56.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قَسْوَرَةٍ): القسورة is the band of archers who hunt them [i.e. the wild asses]; it has also been said: the lion. One says ليوث قساور ("lions, overpowering ones"). It is of the pattern فعولة [Translator's note: so in the source; the pattern of قسورة is فَعْوَلة] from القسر, which is overpowering and conquest, and on its measure is الحيدرة, one of the names of the lion. In al-Mukhtār: «القسور and القسورة: the lion». In al-Qāmūs: «القسورة: the mighty one, and the lion, like القسور; the middle of the night, or its beginning, or most of it; a lowland plant; the plural is قسور; and the archers among hunters, the singular being قسور». His commentator, al-Tāj, followed this up by saying: «His saying "the singular being قسور": al-Layth said so, and it is an error; قسور is not pluralized as قسورة. Rather القسورة is a collective noun for the archers, with no singular from its own root». Abū Ḥayyān's wording: «القسورة: the archers and hunters, as Ibn Kaysān said; or the lion, as a number of the lexicographers said. He said:
مضمر تحدره الأبطال ... كأنه القسورة الريبال
(Lean-bellied, the heroes draw back from him, as if he were the overpowering lion.)
Or the strong men; Labīd said:
إذا ما هتفنا هتفة في ندينا ... أتانا الرجال الصائدون القساور
(Whenever we raise a cry in our assembly, there come to us the men, the hunters, the overpowering ones.)
Or the darkness of the beginning of the night, not the darkness of its end, as Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Thaʿlab said».

* I'rab:
(كَلَّا وَالْقَمَرِ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ): كلا is a particle of deterrence and rebuke to whoever denies that it is one of the great things, a warning to mankind. The wāw is a particle of oath and genitive; القمر is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم. There is no sense in what al-Jalāl said: «كلا is an opening particle meaning ألا», nor in what al-Qurṭubī said, quoting al-Farrāʾ: «it is a connective of the oath, its implied form being إي والقمر». والليل is a preposition and its genitive noun, the wāw being for oath. إذ is an adverb (ẓarf) for past time attached to the verb of oath, and the clause أدبر is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.
(وَالصُّبْحِ إِذا أَسْفَرَ): the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive; الصبح is genitive by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم. إذا is an adverb of time attached to the omitted verb of oath, and the clause أسفر is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.
(إِنَّها لَإِحْدَى الْكُبَرِ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and إحدى الكبر is the khabar (predicate) of إنها.
(نَذِيراً لِلْبَشَرِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إحدى الكبر. Al-Zamakhsharī parsed it as a tamyīz (specification) from إحدى الكبر, in the sense that it is one of the calamities in respect of warning, as you say: "she is one of the women in chastity". We quote below the words of al-Samīn and of Abū al-Baqāʾ and leave the choice to you. «His saying, the Exalted, «نذيرا للبشر», has several aspects. First, that it is a tamyīz from إحدى, because of the sense of magnification it contains, as though it were said: the greatest of the great things in warning; so نذير means الإنذار (warning). Second, that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) also meaning الإنذار, but accusative by an implied verb, as al-Farrāʾ said. Third, that it is فعيل in the sense of مُفعِل (warner), and is a ḥāl from the pronoun in إنها, as al-Zajjāj said. Fourth, that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in إحدى, because of the sense of magnification it contains, as though it were said: the greatest of the great things, warning. Fifth, that it is a ḥāl from the agent of قم فأنذر at the beginning of the sūra. Sixth, that it is a maṣdar, accusative by أنذر at the beginning of the sūra. Seventh, that it is a ḥāl from الكبر. Eighth, that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of الكبر. Ninth, that it is a ḥāl from إحدى الكبر, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya said. Tenth, that it is accusative by a concealed أعني ("I mean"). Other things have also been said». As for Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording, it is: «His saying, the Exalted, نذيرا: there are several aspects to its accusative. First, it is a ḥāl from the agent in His saying قم at the beginning of the sūra. Second, from the pronoun in فأنذر, as an emphasizing ḥāl. Third, it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in إحدى. Fourth, it is a ḥāl from إحدى itself. Fifth, a ḥāl from الكبر or from the pronoun in it. Sixth, a ḥāl from the noun of إنّ. Seventh, that نذيرا has the sense of إنذارا, i.e. "so warn with a warning", or "it is one of the great things for the warning of mankind". Among these views are some we do not approve, but we have related them. The preferred view is that it is a ḥāl from what the clause indicates, its implied form being "it has become great upon him [Translator's note: so in the source; «عليه» does not appear in Abū Ḥayyān's quotation below] as a warning"». As for Abū Ḥayyān, after citing these aspects he said: «Abū al-Baqāʾ said: the preferred view is that it is a ḥāl from what the clause indicates, its implied form being "it has become great as a warning"; and this is a view with no harm in it». نذيرٌ was also read in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a warning".
(لِمَنْ شاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ): لمن is a badal (substitute) of His saying للبشر with repetition of the preposition. The clause شاء has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. منكم is a ḥāl. أن and what lies within its scope are in the position of accusative by شاء, and the agent of شاء refers to من. It has also been said that the agent is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, i.e. "for whomever He — Allah the Exalted — wills". Al-Zamakhsharī said: أن يتقدم is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and لمن شاء is a khabar fronted before it, as in your saying لمن توضأ أن يصلي ("whoever has made ablution may pray"). Its meaning is: it is open to whoever wills to advance or lag behind that he advance or lag behind; and what is meant by advancing is hastening to good, and by lagging behind, falling back from it. It is like His saying: فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر. End of quotation. This is a meaning that does not come readily to mind, and there is ellipsis in it.
(كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ): a resumptive statement to make clear that every soul is pledged for what it has earned. كل نفس is a mubtadaʾ; بما is attached to رهينة; the clause كسبت has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما; رهينة is the khabar. It is a maṣdar meaning رهن ("pledge"), like الشتيمة meaning الشتم ("insult"). It is not in the sense of a passive participle, because [if it were] it would be without tāʾ: had the adjective been intended, رهين would have been said, since فعيل in the sense of مفعول is the same for masculine and feminine. From it is the verse of the Ḥamāsa:
أبعد الذي بالنعف نعف كويكب ... رهينة رمس ذي تراب وجندل
أأذكر بالبقيا على من أصابني ... وبقياي أني جاهد غير مؤتل
(After the one at the hillside, the hillside of Kuwaykib, pledged to a grave of earth and stones — shall I be spoken of for sparing the one who struck me, when my sparing is that I strive, unsparing?)
The two verses are by Ziyād ibn Musawwar [Translator's note: so in the source] al-Ḥārithī; it has also been said by ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd, whose father Ziyād [Translator's note: so in the source; the names do not match] was killed, and seven blood-monies were offered to him for him, but he refused anything but vengeance. The question is a denial (inkārī). النعف, with fatḥa, is the mountain and the raised place; it has also been said: what faces you of the mountain. Kuwaykib is a particular mountain. In this substitution there is detail after summary, which signals the gravity of the place and the state, i.e. "after the killing of my father, buried in that place, in the state of being confined in a grave". It has also been said: رهينةِ in the genitive as a substitute of الذي, so it is a noun attached to the nouns (al-jawāmid) [Translator's note: the source has «الجواحد», evidently a misprint for «الجوامد»] meaning الرهن. One says رمست الشيء رمسا when you bury it in earth; the maṣdar was used and its place, the grave, was meant. الجندل is stones. The interrogative hamza was repeated in أأذكر as an emphasis of the first, because it too enters this verb implicitly. It may also be that it enters an implied verb, i.e. "after my father, shall I rejoice in the blood-money?". البقيا is sparing something, i.e. I will not be spoken of among people as having spared my father's killer, while my sparing of him is that I strive, or am resolved, to assassinate him, not swearing to it, because I do not need to swear in carrying out my affairs; or "not falling short in striving", because الائتلاء comes in the sense of swearing and in the sense of falling short.
(إِلَّا أَصْحابَ الْيَمِينِ): إلا is a particle of exception and أصحاب اليمين is the excepted (mustathnā). It has been said to be connected (muttaṣil), because Allah the Exalted made the obligations of His servants like a debt upon them, and their souls are under His dominion and power, so they are pledged; whoever pays the debt he was charged with frees his soul from the punishment of Allah the Exalted, which has been put in the place of the sign of the pledge, namely its being taken for the debt, and whoever does not pay is punished. It has also been said to be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), since those meant by them are the children, because they have no deeds by which they could be pledged; it has also been said: the angels.
(فِي جَنَّاتٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ): في جنات is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are in Gardens", and the clause is resumptive, as though it arose as an answer to a question arising from the exception, its implied form being: "what is their affair and state?". The clause يتساءلون is a second khabar. Abū al-Baqāʾ chose that في جنات be a ḥāl from أصحاب اليمين, and that it be a ḥāl from the pronoun in يتساءلون, and that it be attached to يتساءلون, making it an adverb of the verb. The meaning of يتساءلون is: they ask one another. عن المجرمين is attached to يتساءلون, and a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "about the state of the criminals".
(ما سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ): the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. "saying", so the clause of saying is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, the question being for rebuke and wonder at their state; the clause سلككم is the khabar, and في سقر is attached to it.
(قالُوا لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ): قالوا is a verb and its agent; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [to the past] and jussive; نك is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the implied sukūn on the nūn that was omitted for lightening, since it is omitted from the jussive imperfect of كان when it is not followed by a vowelless letter; its like has preceded. The noun of نك is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن, and من المصلين is its khabar.
(وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ): conjoined to the previous clause, matching it in its i'rab.
(وَكُنَّا نَخُوضُ مَعَ الْخائِضِينَ): conjoined to what precedes. كان and its noun; the clause نخوض is its khabar; مع is an adverb of place attached to نخوض, and الخائضين is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e. we would plunge into falsehood with those who plunge. This is a warning to everyone whose soul tempts him to hasten to answer about what he does not know.
(وَكُنَّا نُكَذِّبُ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ): also conjoined to what precedes.
(حَتَّى أَتانَا الْيَقِينُ): حتى is a particle of limit and genitive; أتانا اليقين is a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent. The limit applies to the four matters just mentioned.
(فَما تَنْفَعُهُمْ شَفاعَةُ الشَّافِعِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is negative; تنفعهم is an imperfect verb and a direct object; شفاعة الشافعين is the agent. The meaning is that there is no intercession for them; more on its meaning will come in the Rhetoric section.
(فَما لَهُمْ عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; ما is an interrogative noun of denial in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; لهم is the khabar; عن التذكرة is attached to معرضين, and معرضين is a ḥāl from the pronoun made genitive by the lām. Whoever made it a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the khabar erred, because that pronoun refers to ما, which denotes a thing or cause, whereas معرضين describes the persons themselves, so it cannot properly be a description of the causes of turning away, according to the rule that the ḥāl is a description of the one it qualifies.
(كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ): the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) from the pronoun latent in معرضين, so it is an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl. كأنّ and its noun; حمر is its khabar and مستنفرة an adjective. It was read among the Seven with kasra and with fatḥa on the fāʾ: the first means "fleeing", and the second means "put to flight" by the lion or the hunter.
(فَرَّتْ مِنْ قَسْوَرَةٍ): the clause is a second adjective of حمر. فرت is a past verb, and the agent is latent, referring to the asses; the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; من قسورة is attached to فرت.
(بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُؤْتى صُحُفاً مُنَشَّرَةً): بل is a transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī) away from something omitted, which is the answer to the previous question, as though it were said: they have no answer to this question, i.e. they have no reason for turning away; rather, each of them wants…. يريد is an imperfect verb, nominative; كل امرئ is the agent; منهم is an adjective. أن and what lies within its scope are in the position of accusative as a direct object. يؤتى is a passive imperfect verb, and its deputy agent is latent, its implied form being هو; صحفا is a second object, and منشرة is an adjective of صحفا, i.e. spread open, not rolled up, so that everyone who sees them reads them.
(كَلَّا بَلْ لا يَخافُونَ الْآخِرَةَ): كلا is a deterrent from this wish; بل is a transitional digression to make clear the cause of this obstinacy; لا is negative; يخافون الآخرة is an imperfect verb, its agent and its direct object.
(كَلَّا إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ): كلا is a deterrent from turning away. إنّ and its noun, i.e. the Qurʾān, and تذكرة is its khabar.
(فَمَنْ شاءَ ذَكَرَهُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; شاء is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the object of شاء is omitted, its implied form being "to remember it". ذكره is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
(وَما يَذْكُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ هُوَ أَهْلُ التَّقْوى وَأَهْلُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; يذكرون is an imperfect verb and its agent; إلا is a particle of exception; أن يشاء الله — the maṣdar — is an exception from the most general of states: He made the negation of remembrance absolute and then excepted from it the state of the absolute will. هو is a mubtadaʾ and أهل التقوى its khabar, and أهل المغفرة is conjoined to أهل التقوى.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying, the Exalted, «فما تنفعهم شفاعة الشافعين» there is a device alluded to before, namely «negating a thing by affirming it». It is that the speaker affirms something on the surface of his words, on condition that what is affirmed is borrowed, and then negates figuratively what is from its cause, while what is negated in reality is in the inner sense of the speech. We spoke of it at length in al-Baqara at His saying لا يسألون الناس إلحافا, and in Ghāfir at His saying «ولا شفيع يطاع». Here is a clearer definition: it is that you say something whose surface indicates that it negates an attribute of something described, while it negates the described thing altogether. The rhetoricians customarily illustrate it with the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
على لاحب لا يهتدى بمناره ... إذا سافه العود الديافي جرجرا
(Upon a well-trodden road whose waymarks give no guidance; when the old Dayāfī camel sniffs it, he groans.)
His saying لا يهتدى بمناره [Translator's note: the source here writes «لمناره»] would mean that it has waymarks but they give no guidance; yet that is not what is meant. Rather, what is meant is that it has no waymarks to be guided by. Likewise here, the meaning is not that people intercede for them and the intercession of those who intercede does not benefit them; the meaning is only the negation of intercession, so benefit is negated, i.e. there is no intercession of intercessors for them that could benefit them — of the type «على لاحب لا يهتدى بمناره», i.e. it has no waymarks by which to be guided. And singling them out by the negation of the intercession of intercessors indicates that there may be intercessions from which benefit is derived.
2- In His saying «كأنهم حمر مستنفرة، فرّت من قسورة» there is an unrestricted simile (tashbīh mursal): He likened them to asses put to flight. In this there is plain censure, a disparagement of their state and a testimony against them of foolishness and lack of intelligence. You see nothing like the flight of wild asses and their headlong running when something alarms them.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُدَّثِّرُ﴾.
He means: the one who has covered himself with his garments in order to sleep.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَرْنِي وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وَحِيداً﴾.
There are two ways in [الوحيد]. Some said: leave Me [alone] with him whom I created by Myself alone. Others said: I created him alone, having neither wealth nor sons; and this is the more comprehensive of the two ways.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالاً مَّمْدُوداً﴾.
Al-Kalbī said: goods, gold and silver. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] Muḥammad told us, he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told me, from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muhājir, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالاً مَّمْدُوداً﴾; he said: a thousand dinars. We think that "extended" (mamdūd) was used for the number because a thousand is the limit of number: from a thousand one goes back to the beginning of counting. Similar to it is the Arabs' saying: لك على ألف أقدع (I owe you a full thousand), i.e. the limit of number.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَبَنِينَ شُهُوداً﴾.
He had ten sons who were never absent from his sight, either for trade or for work. And "the one alone" is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ﴾.
