They mention that he gathered the chiefs of the people of Mecca and said: The season [of pilgrimage] has drawn near, and the affair of this man has spread among the people; what will you say about him to the people? They said: We will say: [he is] mad. He said: Then people will come to him and speak with him, and he will be seen to be sane and sound, and they will call you liars. They said: We will say: a poet. He said: They are Arabs who have transmitted poems and know them, and Muḥammad's speech does not resemble poetry. They said: We will say: a soothsayer. He said: They know the soothsayers [112/b] and have questioned them, and they do not say: such and such will happen, if Allah wills; whereas Muḥammad tells you nothing without saying: if Allah wills. Then he stood up, and they said: al-Walīd has turned Sabian (ṣabaʾa) — meaning: al-Walīd has become Muslim. His nephew Abū Jahl said: I will deal with him for you. He went to him and said: Quraysh claim that you have turned Sabian, and they want to collect for you wealth that will suffice you in place of what you want to eat of the leftovers of Muḥammad's ﷺ companions. He said: Woe to you! By Allah, they never have their fill, so how would I seek their leftovers when I am the wealthiest of Quraysh? But I have been thinking about the affair of Muḥammad ﷺ, and what we should answer the Arabs when they ask us; and I have resolved to say: a sorcerer. This is the interpretation of His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ﴾: [he reflected and determined] what to say about Muḥammad ﷺ.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾.
قُتل, that is: he was cursed. Likewise ﴿قاتلهم الله﴾ and ﴿قُتِلَ الإِنْسَانُ ما أَكْفَرَهُ﴾: it is mentioned that these [mean] cursing.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ﴾.
He means: arise and pray, and command [others] to pray.

farraa:21-22.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ نَظَرَ ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ﴾.
They mention that he passed by a group of Muslims in the Sacred Mosque, and they said: Will you come to Islam, O Abū al-Mughīra? He said: Your companion is nothing but a sorcerer, and his speech is nothing but sorcery that he learned from Musaylima the Liar and from the sorcerers of Babylon. Then — He said — he turned away from them in arrogance, having frowned and scowled: he grimaced, too proud to believe.

farraa:24-24.t: That is His saying: ﴿إِنْ هَذَآ إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ﴾: he transmits it from the people of Babylon.

farraa:26-26.t:
Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ﴾.
It is one of the names of Hell; for that reason it is not made fully declinable (lam yujra), and likewise "لظى".

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾.
It is joined back to سقر with the intention of repetition, as He said: ﴿ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ﴾, and as He said in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَهَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخاً﴾. Had it been "لواحةً للبشر" [in the accusative], it would be correct,
as He said: ﴿إِنَّهَا لإِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ(35) نَذِيراً لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾ (36). In the reading of Ubayy: "نذِيرٌ لِلْبشَر"; and all are correct.
[Translator's note: «وَهَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخاً» is as printed; this is the standard reading, and the reading of ʿAbd Allāh usually cited at this point is «شيخٌ».]
His saying: ﴿لَوَّاحَةٌ لِِّلْبَشَرِ﴾.
It blackens the skin (al-bashara) by burning it.

farraa:30-31.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَيْهَا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ﴾.
The Arabs give fatḥa to [the numbers] from أحد عشر to تسعة عشر in the genitive and the nominative [alike]. Some of them lighten the ʿayn in تسعة عشر, giving the ʿayn sukūn in the masculine; but they do not lighten it in ثلاث عشرة to تسع عشرة, because they only lightened [it] in the masculine because of the large number of vowels. As for the feminine, the shīn of عشْرة has sukūn, so they did not lighten its ʿayn, lest two quiescent letters meet. Likewise اثنا عشر in the masculine: the ʿayn is not lightened, because the alif of اثنا عشر is quiescent, so another letter is not given sukūn after it, lest two quiescent letters meet.
[Translator's note: «خفضوا» ("put in the genitive") is as printed; in context it means «خففوا» ("lightened").]
One of the unbelievers of the people of Mecca, namely Abū Jahl, said: And what are nineteen? A man among us can overpower one and keep him off the people. And a man of Banū Jumaḥ, whose kunya was Abū al-Ashaddayn, said: I will take care of seventeen for you; you take care of two for me. So Allah sent down: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَآ أَصْحَابَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلاَّ مَلاَئِكَةً﴾, i.e.: and who can overpower the angels? Then He said: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ ﴾ in its smallness ﴿إِلاَّ فِتْنَةً﴾ for those who disbelieve, so that they would say what they said. Then He said: ﴿لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾: certainty added to their certainty, because the number of the keepers of Hell in their Book is nineteen; ﴿وَيَزْدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِيمَاناً﴾ because it is likewise in the Book of the People of the Book.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read it: "والليل إذَا دَبر", and Mujāhid and some of the people of Medina likewise; and many people read it: "واللَّيْل إذْ أَدْبَر". [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl told me that, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Zayd, that he read it: "والليل إذْ أَدْبَر". In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "والليل إذا أدبر", and al-Ḥasan read it likewise: "إذا أدبر", as ʿAbd Allāh did.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told me, from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from a man — I know him only as al-Agharr — from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: "والليل إذا دَبَر".
And he said: أدبر is only [said of] the back of a camel [i.e. being galled]. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told us, from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from Abū ʿAṭiyya, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he read "أدبر". [Al-Farrāʾ said: I think Abū ʿAṭiyya can only be al-Wādiʿī — indeed it is he. And al-Farrāʾ said: there is no إذ in Qays's report, and I consider the two only as two dialect forms.] One says: دبر النساء (sic), and the winter and the summer أدبر (went away); and likewise قَبَل and أقبل. But when they say: أقبل الراكب وأدبر (the rider came and went), they say it only with alif. To me the two are one in meaning; I do not rule out that what occurs with time-periods may occur with men.
[Translator's note: «دبر النساء» is as printed; «الشتاء» ("winter") or similar appears to be intended.]

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهَا لإِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ﴾.
The هاء is a pronoun standing for Hell.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿نَذِيراً لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾.
One of the grammarians used to say: "نذيراً" is accusative [by] the beginning of the sura: O Muḥammad, arise as a warner to mankind. That is nothing, and Allah knows best, because much speech has come in between them, and its nominative in the reading of Ubayy rules out this meaning. Its accusative [rather] comes from His saying: ﴿إِنَّها لإحدى الكُبر نذيراً﴾: you detach it (taqṭaʿuhu) from the definite, because "إحدى الكبر" is definite, so you detached it from it [making it a ḥāl (circumstantial)]. Its accusative may also be by making النذير mean "warning", from His saying: ﴿لاَ تُبْقِى وَلاَ تَذَرُ﴾ لواحة [— you tell this about Hell as a warning] to mankind; for نذير may have the meaning of إنذار (warning). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿كَيْفَ نَذِير﴾ and ﴿فَكَيْفَ كان نكِير﴾, meaning: My warning and My reproach.

farraa:39-42.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾.
Al-Kalbī said: they are the people of Paradise. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ told me, from Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, from al-Minhāl, tracing it back to ʿAlī, who said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾ — he said: they are the children. This seems right, because the children have not earned anything for which they would be held in pledge; and in His saying: ﴿يَتَسَآءَلُونَ عَنِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ﴾ there is what strengthens [the view] that they are the children, because they did not know sins, so they asked: ﴿مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ﴾.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾.
He is saying: do not be treacherous and so defile your garments, for the treacherous man is "soiled of garments". It is also said: "and purify your garments" [means] and set right your deeds. Some said: "and purify your garments" means: shorten them, for shortening garments is purification.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلرُّجْزَ فَٱهْجُرْ﴾.
ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan read it with kasra [الرِّجز], and al-Sulamī, Mujāhid and the people of Medina read it with ḍamma, reading: "والرجزُ فاهجر". Mujāhid explained: الرجز means the idols; and al-Kalbī explained it: الرجز is the punishment. We think that they are two dialect forms and that the meaning in both [112/a] is one.
[Translator's note: the source writes «والرجزُ» with a ḍamma on the zāy, while the point under discussion is the vowel of the rāʾ (الرُّجز).]

farraa:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُّسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it: "مستنفِرة" with kasra, and the people of the Hijaz read it: "مستنفَرة" with fatḥa on the fāʾ; both are frequent in the speech of the Arabs. The poet said:
أمْسِكْ حِمارَكَ إِنَّهُ مُسْتنفِرٌ * فى إِثرِ أحْمِرَةٍ عَمْدنَ لِغُرّبِ
(Hold back your donkey, for it is bolting after she-asses that have made for Ghurrab.)
As for القسورة, it is said that it is the archers; and al-Kalbī said, with his chain of transmission: it is the lion.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ told me, from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq, [father of] Abū Sufyān al-Thawrī, from ʿIkrima, who said: It was said to him: القسورة is the lion in the language of the Abyssinians. He said: القسورة are the archers; the lion in the language of the Abyssinians is ʿanbasa.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفاً مُّنَشَّرَةً﴾.
The unbelievers of Quraysh said to the Prophet ﷺ [114/a]: When a man among the Children of Israel committed a sin, his sin would be found written on a sheet in the morning; so why do we not see that? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفاً مُّنَشَّرَةً﴾.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾.
He means this Qur'an. Had it been said: "إنها تذكرةٌ", it would be correct, as He said in [Sūrat] ʿAbasa. Whoever says (إنها) means the sura, and whoever says (إنه) means the Qur'an.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾.
He is saying: do not give anything in this world in order to receive more than it. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ولا تَمْنُن أنْ تَسْتَكْثِرَ", and this is evidence for the indicative (rafʿ) in "تستكثر". Had it been made jussive with this meaning, it would be correct; but the indicative is the way of the reading and of practice.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي ٱلنَّاقُورِ﴾.
It is said that it is the first of the two blasts.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «فأنذر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «قم».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); «ربَّك» is the fronted object of «كبر»; the clause «كَبِّر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أنذر».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «ولا تمنن» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «اهجر», and the clause «تستكثر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تمنن».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); the preposition phrase «لربك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اصبر».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the preposition phrase is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e.: when the Trumpet is sounded, the matter becomes hard.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «يومئذ» is a badal (substitute) from «فذلك», and it is made indeclinable because it is annexed to an indeclinable word; «إذٍ» is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the tanwīn is for compensation. His words «عسير»: a naʿt (adjective) of «يوم».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «غير» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «يوم»; the preposition phrase «على الكافرين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {عَسِيرٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «ذرني» is resumptive; «من» is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the yāʾ; «وحيدا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied (muqaddar) pronoun in «خلقت», i.e.: I created him alone.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The preposition phrase «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن أزيد» is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: for increase (في الزيادة).

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The preposition phrase «لآياتنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عنيدا», which includes the meaning of «جاحدا» (denying).

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «سأرهقه» is resumptive; «صعودا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «فقتل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إنه فكر»; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «قدَّر» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: (ثم قتل كيف قدر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding one.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «يؤثر» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سحر».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: (إن هذا إلا قول البشر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «سقر» is a second object, and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «وما أدراك» is parenthetical between the ḥāl (circumstantial) clause and the one possessing it, «سقر»; the clause «ما سقر» is the object of «أدراك», suspended by the interrogative.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «لا تبقي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first «سقر».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «لواحة» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: it is scorching (هي لواحة), and the clause is a second ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first «سقر».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: «تسعة عشر» are two parts, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is a third ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «وما جعلنا» is resumptive; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «ملائكة» is a second object; the preposition phrase «للذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فتنة»; the genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليستيقن» is attached to the second «جعل»; «إيمانا» is tamyīz (specification); «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا» is a relative noun, the khabar (predicate); «مثلا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the demonstrative; the clause «يضل» is resumptive, and the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: Allah leads astray with a leading astray like that leading astray; the clause «وما يعلم» is resumptive; «هو» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يعلم»; and likewise «وما هي إلا ذكرى» [is resumptive]; the preposition phrase «للبشر» is attached to a naʿt of «ذكرى».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «والقمر»: the wāw is for the oath, and the thing sworn by is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) verb «أقسم» (I swear).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The adverb «إذ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb «أقسم».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «إذا» is a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb «أقسم».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: (إنها لإحدى الكبر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: «نذيرا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «إحدى»; the preposition phrase «للبشر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نذيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The preposition phrase «لمن» is a badal (substitute) from «البشر»; the preposition phrase «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَنْ»; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يتقدم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «شاء».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رهينة».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The preposition phrase «في جنات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «يتساءلون».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The clause «ما سلككم» is explicative of the asking.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «نَكُ» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) with the sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the nūn that was omitted for lightness.

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن أتانا) is genitive by «حتى», attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نكذب».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: (فما تنفعهم شفاعة الشافعين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The clause «فما لهم» is resumptive; «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition phrase «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «عن التذكرة» is attached to «مُعْرضين», the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «لهم».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: (كأنهم حمر مستنفرة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in {مُعْرِضِينَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «فَرَّتْ» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {حُمُرٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The clause «يريد» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كل»; the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يؤتى» is the object of «يريد»; «صحفا» is the second object of «يؤتى».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «فمن شاء» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ}; «من» is a conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «وما يذكرون» is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ; and the clause «هو أهل» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the Divine Name.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (المدثر): its origin is (المتدثر) [Translator's note: the printed text has «المندثر»]; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl because they share one point of articulation, and the dāl is stronger than the tāʾ [Translator's note: printed «الثاء»] because it is voiced (majhūra) while the tāʾ is unvoiced (mahmūsa). So both were turned into the stronger of them, since that is a strengthening of the letter; they were not turned into the tāʾ [printed «الناء»] because that would weaken the letter, since turning the stronger into the weaker is a deficiency in the letter and in the pronunciation. Such is the rule for most assimilation between two different letters: the weaker of them is turned into the sound of the stronger.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying (ولا تمنن تستكثر): (تستكثر) is nominative because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "do not give a gift in order to take more than it". It is also said that it is nominative because of the omission of (أن), the implied form being "Do not weaken, O Muhammad, from seeking much of the good"; when (أن) was omitted, it became nominative.
His saying (فإذا نقر في الناقور): [(في الناقور)] stands in the place of the one whose agent is not named [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. It is also said [Translator's note: printed «وقبل», read as «وقيل»] that the maṣdar (verbal noun) is implied and stands in the place of the agent.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (فذلك يومئذ): (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (يومئذ) is a badal (substitute) from it, and (يوم عسير) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (عسير) is a naʿt (adjective) of (يوم), and likewise (غير يسير) is also a naʿt of (يوم). It is also said that (يومئذ) is accusative with an implied "I mean" (أعني).

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying (ذرني ومن خلقت): (من) is in the position of the accusative by conjunction with the nūn and yāʾ, or it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).
His saying (وحيدا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied hāʾ in (خلقت), i.e. "I created him alone".
His saying (وجعلت له مالا ممدودا): (له) is in the position of the second object of (جعلت), because it means "made" (صيّرت) and takes two objects.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying (وبنين شهودا): its singular is (ابن). The connective alif was dropped in the plural and the bāʾ took a vowel only because the plural returns a thing to its origin, and its origin is (بني) on the pattern faʿal. When it was pluralised it was returned to its origin, so they said (بنين). When the yāʾ, which is the final radical, took a vowel and what precedes it had fatḥa, [it turned into] an alif, and it was dropped because it was vowelless and the yāʾ of the plural after it was vowelless; and the letter before the yāʾ was given kasra according to the original pattern of the plural yāʾ in the accusative and genitive. It should properly have kept what precedes it with fatḥa, to indicate the departed alif, as they said (مصطفين) and (أعلين); but (ابن) ran in its weak-letter treatment in the singular contrary to analogy: it should properly have been like (عصا) and (رحى), with no connective alif entering it and its first letter not vowelless. So since it departed from its origin in the singular, it also departed in the plural from the principles of the weak-letter rules, because the plural is a branch after the singular. In the relative adjective (nisba) of it they said (بنوي), returning it to its origin; the origin of this wāw is an alif changed from a yāʾ, which is the final radical. Sībawayh allowed the nisba on its own wording, allowing (ابني), and others disallowed it.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t:
His saying (وما أدراك ما سقر): the discussion of it has already preceded, since it is like (وما أدراك ما الحاقة).
His saying (ولا تذر): the wāw was dropped only because it was construed on its counterpart in usage and meaning, namely (تدع), since it has its meaning, and because no past tense is used from either of them. So (تذر) was construed on (تدع), and its first radical was dropped as it was dropped in (تدع). It was dropped in (تدع) only because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra, since the fatḥa of the dāl is incidental: it took fatḥa only because of the guttural letter, and kasra is its origin; so the word was built on its origin and that was presumed in it, and the wāw of (تدع) was dropped for that reason. (تذر) was construed on it because it has its meaning and resembles it in that the past tense of both is not used.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t:
His saying (لواحة): nominative with an implied "it is" (هي لواحة).
(سقر) is a diptote because it is a definite feminine noun.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying (عليها تسعة عشر): (تسعة عشر) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (عليها) is the khabar (predicate). They are two nouns between which the conjunction was omitted and which contain it, so they were made indeclinable (mabnī) because they contain the meaning of the particle; they were made indeclinable on fatḥa because of its lightness. It is also said that they were made indeclinable on the fatḥa that belonged to the omitted wāw. Al-Farrāʾ allowed in speech making the ʿayn vowelless in the numbers from thirteen to nineteen.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t:
His saying, the Exalted: (أصحاب): the plural of (صاحب) with the augment of (صاحب) dropped, as if it were the plural of (صحب), like (كتف) and (أكتاف).
His saying (ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا): if you make (ما) and (ذا) one noun, it is in the position of the accusative governed by (أراد). If you make (ذا) mean (الذي), then (ما) is an interrogative, a complete noun, nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ذا) is the khabar (predicate); (أراد) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ذا) and the hāʾ is omitted from it, i.e. "What is that which Allah intended by this?", in the sense "What thing is that which Allah intended by this as an example?" (مثلا) is accusative as an explanation (bayān).
His saying (كذلك يضل الله من يشاء): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying (إنها لإحدى الكبر): it is not permissible to drop the alif and lām from (الكبر) and from what is like it, except (أخر), from which the alif and lām have been dropped while it contains their meaning, so it became definite by containing their meaning; that is why it is a diptote even in the indefinite. It is deflected (maʿdūl) from the alif and lām.

mekki-muskil:36-36.t: His saying (نذيرا للبشر): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (قم) in His saying (قم فأنذر); this is the view of al-Kisāʾī. It is also said that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in (إنها); also said: from (إحدى); also said: from (هو). It is also said that it is accusative with an implied verb, i.e. "Allah made it a warner", i.e. possessing warning, so the word is masculine by way of attribution (nasab). It is also said that it is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a warning possessing warning", so the word is masculine by way of attribution. It is also said that it is in the position of the maṣdar, i.e. "a warning to mankind", as He said (فكيف كان نكير), i.e. "My disapproval of them". [Translator's note: the source repeats part of this passage, apparently a copying error; translated as written.] It is also said that it is accusative with an implied "I mean" (أعني).

mekki-muskil:46-46.t: His saying (وكنا نكذب) and (وكنا نخوض): the kāf was given ḍamma in this, and in the first letter of whatever is like it, such as (قمنا) and (قلنا), although the origin of all of it is fatḥa, so that the ḍamma would indicate that it was transferred from faʿala to faʿula. It is also said: it was given ḍamma only to indicate that it is among the verbs with wāw; and it is also said: to indicate that the dropped letter is a wāw. Both of these views fall away because they give kasra to the first letter of (خفت), which has wāw as its middle radical like (كان), and whose dropped letter is a wāw in the [verb of] choice, like the dropped letter of (قمت), (قلت) and (كنت). Their giving kasra to the first letter of (خفت) shows that they gave kasra only to indicate that it is from faʿila, with kasra on the ʿayn. As for their giving kasra to the first letter of (بعت), it is to indicate that it was transferred from faʿala to faʿila, and to indicate that it is among the verbs with yāʾ and that the dropped letter is a yāʾ. Because these reasons come together, ḍamma and kasra occur on the first letter of that; so know it.

mekki-muskil:56-56.t: His saying (وما يذكرون إلا أن يشاء الله): the object of (يذكرون) is omitted, i.e. "they do not remember anything". (أن) is in the position of the accusative as an exception, or in the position of the genitive with the preposition implied. The object of (يشاء) is omitted, i.e. "unless Allah wills it".

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle.
﴿أيها﴾: the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda); and هـا is for drawing attention (tanbīh).
﴿المدثر﴾: an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿قم﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿فأنذر﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أنذر is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "you" (أنت); and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وربك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the word رب is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is muḍāf, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿فكبر﴾: the fāʾ is linking, for an implied condition; and كبر is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وثيابك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ثياب is a fronted object, and it is muḍāf, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿فطهر﴾: the fāʾ is linking, for an implied condition; and طهر is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿والرجز﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الرجز is a fronted object.
﴿فاهجر﴾: the fāʾ is linking, for an implied condition; and اهجر is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is prohibitive (nāhiya).
﴿تمنن﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿تستكثر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "you" (أنت); and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ولربك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is a preposition, and رب is a genitive noun; it is muḍāf, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اصبر﴾.
﴿فاصبر﴾: the fāʾ is linking, for an implied condition; and اصبر is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿فإذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and إذا is an adverb for future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what the response indicates, because the meaning is: "when the trumpet is sounded, the matter becomes hard for the disbelievers".
﴿نقر﴾: a past verb, built for other than the agent (passive).
﴿في الناقور﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نقر﴾; and the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿فذلك﴾: the fāʾ: linking, for the response of ﴿إذا﴾; and ذلك: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; the reference is to the time of the sounding.
﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative; it is indeclinable because it is annexed to a non-declinable word, namely ﴿إذ﴾. And إذٍ: a noun indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for a clause, the implied form being: "that, on the day when the Trumpet is blown, is a hard day". [Translator's note: so in the source («نفخ في الصور»); the wording of this ayah is ﴿نقر في الناقور﴾.]
﴿يوم﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿عسير﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿يوم﴾, nominative.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿على الكافرين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عسير﴾.
﴿غير﴾: a second naʿt (adjective) of يوم, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; and it is muḍāf.
﴿يسير﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿ذرني﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya); the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت); and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ومن﴾: the wāw is for accompaniment (maʿiyya), and مَن: mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); or the wāw is a conjunction, and مَن is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object in ذرني.
﴿خلقت﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to the tāʾ of the agent; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The referential pronoun is omitted, i.e.: "whom I created".
﴿وحيدا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referential pronoun, accusative (manṣūb). It has also been said: a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun in ذرني, or from the tāʾ in خلقت.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وجعلت﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded; جعلت is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the tāʾ of the agent.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, which is the second object.
﴿مالا﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿ممدودا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿مالا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿وبنين﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿مالا﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ, because it is treated like the sound masculine plural.
﴿شهودا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿بنين﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿ومهدت﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded; مهدت is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the tāʾ of the agent.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مهدت﴾.
﴿تمهيدا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay (tarākhī).
﴿يطمع﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جعلت and مهدت; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿أن﴾: a subjunctive particle.
﴿أزيد﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by ﴿أن﴾, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being: "I" (أنا); and أن with what falls within its scope is construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يطمع﴾.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿إنه﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun); and inna with what follows is a causal (taʿlīliyya) clause.
﴿كان﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb; the ism of kāna is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the clause كان is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿لآياتنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عنيدا﴾.
﴿عنيدا﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿سأرهقه﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future, and أرهقه is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "I" (أنا); and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿صعودا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, because أرهقه contains the meaning of أكلفه ("I will burden him with"). If أرهقه does not contain the meaning of أكلفه, then ﴿صعودا﴾ is in the place of the accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e.: "I will distress him with hardship".

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿إنه﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿فكر﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the clause ﴿فكر﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿وقدر﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿فكر﴾; it is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿فقتل﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and قتل is a past verb whose agent is not named (passive), its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun, accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in قدر.
﴿قدر﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence and delay (tarākhī).
﴿قتل﴾: a past verb whose agent is not named (passive), its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun, accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in قدر.
﴿قدر﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence and delay (tarākhī).
﴿نظر﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence and delay (tarākhī).
﴿عبس﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿وبسر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and بسر is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو).

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence and delay (tarākhī).
﴿أدبر﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿واستكبر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and استكبر is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿فقال﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (قال is) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿إن﴾: negating.
﴿هذا﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿سحر﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿يؤثر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, whose agent is not named (passive); its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being: "it" (هو); and the clause is an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿سحر﴾.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿إن﴾: negating.
﴿هذا﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿قول﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ); and it is muḍāf.
﴿البشر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿سأصليه﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future, and أصليه is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied ḍamma because of heaviness; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "I" (أنا); and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿سقر﴾: second mafʿūl bihi; and the whole clause is a badal (substitute) of His saying: ﴿سأرهقه صعودا﴾.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ما.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿سقر﴾: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause ﴿ما سقر﴾ stands in, in the position of the accusative, in place of the second and third objects of the verb ﴿أدراك﴾, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from operating by the interrogative. And the clause ﴿وما أدراك ما سقر﴾ is parenthetical with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿تبقي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هي); the object is omitted; and the clause ﴿لا تبقي﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negating.
﴿تذر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "it" (هي); the object is omitted; and the clause ﴿لا تذر﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿لا تبقي﴾.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿لواحة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "it" (هي).
﴿للبشر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لواحة﴾; and the clause is a second ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿عليها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿تسعة عشر﴾: a compound numeral, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa of both parts, in the position of the nominative as the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause is a third ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negating.
﴿جعلنا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to ﴿نا﴾; and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿أصحاب﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); and it is muḍāf.
﴿النار﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿ملائكة﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negating.
﴿جعلنا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to ﴿نا﴾; and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil.
﴿عدتهم﴾: عدة is the first mafʿūl bihi, accusative; it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction.
﴿فتنة﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
﴿للذين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فتنة﴾.
﴿كفروا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿ليستيقن﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl), and يستيقن is an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the second ﴿جعلنا﴾. It has also been said: they are attached to an implied verb, i.e.: "We did that so that … may be certain".
﴿الذين﴾: a relative (noun), indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿أوتوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw; it is built for an unnamed agent (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause أوتوا is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿الكتاب﴾: the second object of ﴿أوتوا﴾, accusative.
﴿ويزداد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and يزداد is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿يستيقن﴾, subjunctive.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative (noun), indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿آمنوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿إيمانا﴾: tamyīz (specification), accusative by the fatḥa.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negating.
﴿يرتاب﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive by conjunction with يستيقن.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative (noun), indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿أوتوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw; it is built for an unnamed agent (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; and the clause ﴿أوتوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿الكتاب﴾: the second object of أوتوا, accusative.
﴿والمؤمنون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and المؤمنون is conjoined to الذين.
﴿وليقول﴾: conjoined to what preceded; the lām is the lām of cause, and (يقول is) an imperfect verb, subjunctive by أن implied optionally after the lām of cause.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative (noun), indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿في قلوبهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿مرض﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause ﴿في قلوبهم مرض﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿والكافرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الكافرون is conjoined, nominative by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿ماذا﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted object of ﴿أراد﴾.
﴿أراد﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿بهذا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أراد﴾.
﴿مثلا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from هذا, accusative; and the clause ﴿ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿كذلك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يضل.
﴿يضل﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
﴿يشاء﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); the referential pronoun is omitted; and the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿ويهدي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and يهدي is an imperfect verb, nominative, conjoined to ﴿يضل﴾.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
﴿يشاء﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو); the referential pronoun is omitted; and the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and ما is negating.
﴿يعلم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative.
﴿جنود﴾: a fronted mafʿūl bihi, accusative; and it is muḍāf.
﴿ربك﴾: رب is muḍāf ilayhi, and it is muḍāf, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction.
﴿هو﴾: the fāʿil of يعلم, nominative; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negating.
﴿هي﴾: a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction.
﴿ذكرى﴾: khabar, nominative by an implied ḍamma because pronouncing it is impossible.
﴿للبشر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ذكرى﴾.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿والقمر﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition, and القمر is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being: "I swear" (أقسم).

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿والليل﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition, and الليل is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being: "I swear" (أقسم).
﴿إذ﴾: an adverb for past time, attached to the implied verb of the oath.
﴿أدبر﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هو); and the clause أدبر is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being put in annexation to it.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿والصبح﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition, and الصبح is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being: "I swear" (أقسم).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of time, attached to the implied verb of the oath.
﴿أسفر﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هو); and the clause ﴿أسفر﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being put in annexation to it.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿إنها﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿ها﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿لإحدى﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and إحدى is the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied ḍamma because pronouncing it is impossible; and it is muḍāf.
﴿الكبر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the clause of the response to the oath.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿نذيرا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun concealed in الكبر, or tamyīz (specification).
﴿للبشر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نذيرا﴾.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿لمن﴾: a badal (substitute) of His saying: ﴿للبشر﴾, with the preposition repeated.
﴿شاء﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the clause شاء is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿منكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle.
﴿يتقدم﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو); and أن with what falls within its scope is in the place of the accusative by ﴿شاء﴾.
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿يتأخر﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive by conjunction with ﴿يتقدم﴾, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the clause has no grammatical position, by conjunction with the ṣila clause.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿كل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); and it is muḍāf.
﴿نفس﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
﴿بما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رهينة﴾.
﴿كسبت﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the fāʿil (agent) is: "it" (هو).
﴿رهينة﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿أصحاب﴾: excepted (mustathnā), accusative (manṣūb); and it is muḍāf.
﴿اليمين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿في جنات﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: "they are in gardens"; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿يتساءلون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is a second khabar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:41-41.t: ﴿عن المجرمين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتساءلون﴾.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿سلككم﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is: "it" (هو); and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿في سقر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سلككم﴾; the clause سلككم is the khabar (predicate); and the clause ما is the object of an omitted saying, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: "saying".

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿نك﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being an implied sukūn on the nūn that was dropped for lightness; and the ism (noun) of نكُ is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being: "we" (نحن).
﴿من المصلين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿ولم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿لم﴾ is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿نك﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being an implied sukūn on the nūn that was dropped for lightness; and the ism (noun) of ﴿نكُ﴾ is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being: "we" (نحن).
﴿نطعم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent, its implied form being: "we" (نحن); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of kāna.
﴿المسكين﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t:
﴿وكنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the clause being conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded; kāna is an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿نخوض﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "we" (نحن); and the clause is in the position of the khabar (predicate) of kāna.
﴿مع﴾: an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نخوض﴾; and it is muḍāf.
﴿الخائضين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:46-46.t:
﴿وكنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the clause being conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded; kāna is an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿نكذب﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "we" (نحن); and the clause is in the position of the khabar (predicate) of kāna.
﴿بيوم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نكذب﴾; and it is muḍāf.
﴿الدين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:47-47.t:
﴿حتى﴾: a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition.
﴿أتانا﴾: a past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿اليقين﴾: postponed fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿فما﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ما is negating.
﴿تنفعهم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the hāʾ is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿شفاعة﴾: postponed fāʿil (agent), nominative; and it is muḍāf.
﴿الشافعين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:49-49.t:
﴿فما﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and ما is an interrogative noun of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate).
﴿عن التذكرة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿معرضين﴾.
﴿معرضين﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun concealed in the khabar; and the clause ﴿فما لهم...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t:
﴿كأنهم﴾: kaʾanna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and هم is its ism (noun).
﴿حمر﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kaʾanna, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿مستنفرة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حمر﴾, nominative; and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun concealed in معرضين.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t:
﴿فرت﴾: فرت is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), referring to the asses (الحمر); and the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine.
﴿من قسورة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فرت﴾; and the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حمر﴾.

muyesser-irab:52-52.t:
﴿بل﴾: transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿يريد﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿كل﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative; and it is muḍāf.
﴿امرئ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
﴿منهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كل﴾.
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle.
﴿يؤتى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive), subjunctive (manṣūb); its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); and أن with what falls within its scope is in the place of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿صحفا﴾: the second mafʿūl bihi of يؤتى.
﴿منشرة﴾: a naʿt of ﴿صحفا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:53-53.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿بل﴾: transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يخافون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿الآخرة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:54-54.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿إنه﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿تذكرة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ).

muyesser-irab:55-55.t:
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿شاء﴾: a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the object is omitted.
﴿ذكره﴾: a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the condition with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:56-56.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negating.
﴿يذكرون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle.
﴿يشاء﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb); and the maṣdar is an exception from the most general of states.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative.
﴿هو﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أهل﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative.
﴿التقوى﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وأهل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and أهل is conjoined (maʿṭūf), nominative; and it is muḍāf.
﴿المغفرة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The original form is المتدثر; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl because they are from the same point of articulation. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: he was covered with a velvet cloth (قطيفة). ʿIkrima said: i.e. "I have covered you (دثّرت) with this matter, so carry it out."

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Qatāda said: i.e. warn of Allah's punishment and His blows against the nations. Abū Jaʿfar said: so the construction according to Qatāda's view is: "warn them of these things", and then this was omitted because it is indicated [by the context].

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: I.e. magnify Him by worshipping Him alone; and it [رَبَّكَ] is accusative by كبّر.

nahhas-irab:4-5.t: وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ (4): [ثِيابَكَ is] accusative by طهّر. وَالرُّجْزَ is accusative by فاهجر. Even if the verbs had the hāʾ [i.e. an object pronoun], the accusative would still be preferable, because the command is better construed with a verb.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: وَلا تَمْنُنْ is jussive (majzūm) because of the prohibition, and the doubling was made overt because the second [nūn] is vowelless. If it were in [ordinary] speech, لا تمنّ would be permissible, with fatḥa, kasra or ḍamma on the nūn. Khaṣīf «[Translator's note: the source has «حصيف»; the narrator from Mujāhid is usually Khuṣayf.]» related from Mujāhid, who said: لا تَمْنُنْ means "do not weaken". Abū Jaʿfar said: it would be taken from المنين, which means "weak", and the construction would be: "and do not weaken from seeking much good" — then «أن» was dropped and the verb put in the nominative. Ibn Zayd said: [it means] do not count it as a favour to people that you convey the message, in order to gain much from them. Abū Jaʿfar said: the most appropriate thing said about the meaning — and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best — is: do not count as a favour your obedience and your conveying of the message, deeming it much; and this is the meaning of al-Ḥasan's view. Abū Jaʿfar said: we said this is more appropriate because it fits the context of the speech better, since the passage contains a warning and a command to patience and to diligence in obedience.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: The deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil; lit. "the noun of that whose agent is not named"), according to Sībawayh, is فِي النَّاقُورِ; and according to Abū al-ʿAbbās it is a latent (mustatir) pronoun indicated by the verb.

nahhas-irab:9-10.t: فَذلِكَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); يَوْمَئِذٍ may be a badal (substitute) from it, and it has fatḥa because it is indeclinable (mabnī), just as مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ [al-Maʿārij: 11] has been read [with fatḥa]; and it may be accusative in the sense "I mean". يَوْمٌ is the khabar (predicate) of the subject; عَسِيرٌ is its naʿt (adjective), and likewise غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: مَنْ is in the position of naṣb (accusative), either as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) or conjoined to the nūn and the yāʾ [of ذَرْنِي]. وَحِيداً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: لَهُ is in the position of the second object.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: Since it [the bāʾ of بَنِينَ] has a vowel, the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was dropped; and on this basis they said in the relative adjective (nisba): بنويّ. Sībawayh permitted «ابنيّ», and some of the Kufans disallowed it.

nahhas-irab:15-16.t: كَلَّا is a rejection of his greed and a deterrent to him. إِنَّهُ كانَ لِآياتِنا عَنِيداً: in the sense of معاند (obstinately opposing).

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً (17): ʿAṭiyya related from Abū Saʿīd from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "He will be made to climb a steep slope; when he puts his hand on it, it melts, and when he puts his foot on it, it melts."

nahhas-irab:18-19.t: إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ (18), i.e. he thought about refuting the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and he went back time after time, considering whether he could refute them; and he is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, without disagreement. Qatāda said: they claim that he thought about what the Prophet brought and said: "By Allah, it is not poetry; it has a sweetness and a grace upon it, and in my view it is nothing but magic." So Allah the Exalted revealed: فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ (19). Abū Jaʿfar said: the view of al-Farrāʾ is that قتل means "he was cursed". Abū Jaʿfar said: according to the speech of the Arabs, قتل must mean "he was destroyed", because one who is killed is destroyed.

nahhas-irab:21-22.t: I.e. he contracted [the skin] between his eyes and frowned, when it became hard for him to refute the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ from the truth وَاسْتَكْبَرَ: so Allah reported of his ignorance that he was too proud to believe in the signs of Allah and His Messenger — after a refutation of what he brought was [not] possible for him «[Translator's note: so in the source («بعد أن يتهيأ له ردّ ما جاء به»); the sense seems to require "after a refutation was not possible for him".]» — yet he was not too proud to prostrate to stones that neither benefit nor harm.

nahhas-irab:24-25.t: فَقالَ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ (24): when he found no argument, he disbelieved; then he said: إِنْ هذا إِلَّا قَوْلُ الْبَشَرِ (25). So he added to his ignorance something that is not hidden, because the Prophet ﷺ had challenged them — and they were Arabs like him — to produce a sūra like it, and they were unable to do so; and if it were the speech of a human being, what was possible for him would have been possible for them.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: It has been said: [سَقَرَ] is a diptote because it is the name of a feminine; and it has been said: because it is a foreign noun. The first is correct, because a foreign noun of three letters is declinable [as a triptote], even if its middle letter is vowelled; and moreover it is an Arabic noun with a derivation: one says سقرته الشمس, when the sun burns him; and السّاقور is a piece of iron that is heated and used to brand the donkey.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: The clause is in the position of naṣb (accusative) by إدراك [i.e. أَدْراكَ], except that what precedes an interrogative does not operate on it «[Translator's note: the source has «لا يعلم فيه», apparently a misprint of «لا يعمل فيه», "does not govern it"; translated accordingly.]».

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: It may be asked: why was the wāw dropped from «تذر», when it is only dropped in «يذر»? «[Translator's note: so in the source; the question is apparently why the wāw is dropped in يذر at all.]» And if it is said: its pattern is يفعل, it will be asked: [then why] the fatḥa, when it contains no guttural letter? The answer was given by Ibn Kaysān: since يذر has the same meaning as يدع, in that no past tense of it is pronounced and the meaning of the two is one, they made it follow it [in form].

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: [لَوَّاحَةٌ is nominative] on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is لوّاحة to البشر", i.e. to the creatures; and it [البشر] may be the plural of بشرة ("skin").

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: [تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ is] in the position of rafʿ (nominative) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), except that it has fatḥa because the conjunction wāw was dropped from it, so it was given its vowel. And it has been said: it was heavy, so it was given the lightest of the vowels, because they are two nouns originally. The grammarians differed on forming the relative adjective (nisba) from the two. The view of Sībawayh and a group of grammarians is that when you form the nisba from the two, you drop the second and form the nisba from the first, so you say تسعيّ; أحدي for أحد عشر, and بعلي in the nisba of بعلبكّ. The other view is that the nisba is formed from both of them together and nothing else, so that one says تسعة عشريّ and بعلبكيّ. Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā rejected the first view and said: they are two nouns that express one meaning, so if you drop the second its meaning is lost; so only the nisba from both together is permissible. He argued from what the grammarians agree on in their saying هذا حبّ رمانيّ and جحر ضبيّ — he attached [the nisba] to the second and did not drop it — and likewise هذا أبو عمريّ. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: this is stronger in the nisba — meaning: هذا تسعة عشريّ, معدي كربيّ and بعلبكيّ. Al-Farrāʾ permitted جاءني أحد عشر with a sukūn on the ʿayn, and likewise from ثلاثة عشر to تسعة عشر; but he does not permit this in اثني عشر, so as not to combine two vowelless letters, nor does he permit it in the feminine, so as not to combine two vowelless letters. Abū Jaʿfar said: what he said is not far-fetched; it has been related from Abū Jaʿfar that he read عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ «[Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowels; the reading meant is apparently تِسْعَةَ عْشَرَ, with a sukūn on the ʿayn.]».

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: أَصْحابَ is the plural of صاحب, with the additional letter dropped, because أفعال is not the plural of فاعل without dropping; and أفعال is the plural of eight patterns, among which are neither فاعل nor فعل «[Translator's note: so in the source; the second pattern may be a different vowelling of فعل that has been lost in print.]». وَما جَعَلْنا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا, i.e. a hardship and a test of devotion, so that they disbelieve; so that they know that Allah is able to strengthen and support these angels. لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ: the lām of kay (purpose), and its origin is that it is the lām of the genitive, because the meaning is: "for the certainty of those who were given the Book". وَيَزْدادَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِيماناً is conjoined to the first, and likewise وَلا يَرْتابَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ. Then the lām was repeated, and if it had not been brought it would have been permissible, in وَلِيَقُولَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ وَالْكافِرُونَ ماذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِهذا مَثَلًا. «ما» is in the position of naṣb (accusative) by أراد, and it and ذا are treated as one thing; but if you make «ذا» mean "which" (الذي), then ما is in the position of rafʿ (nominative) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), ذا is its khabar (predicate), and what comes after it is its ṣila (relative clause). كَذلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ: the kāf is in the position of naṣb as a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar. وَما يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ: [هُوَ is] nominative by يعلم, and the accusative as an exception is not permissible; and likewise وَما هِيَ إِلَّا ذِكْرى لِلْبَشَرِ. Mujāhid said: i.e. the Fire is nothing but a reminder to mankind. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr mentioned that the full stop is at كَلَّا, on the understanding that the meaning is: the matter is not as the polytheist said to his fellow polytheists, "I will deal with the keepers of the Fire for you". وَالْقَمَرِ is an oath, i.e. "by the Lord of the moon".

nahhas-irab:33-34.t: ] «[Translator's note: the source begins with a stray bracket, and the first reading being described has dropped out of the text; it is presumably وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا دَبَرَ.]» is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; and al-Ḥasan, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ḥamza and Nāfiʿ read وَاللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ. Abū Jaʿfar said: the correct view is that دبر and أدبر have the same meaning; this is what the exegetes and most of the lexicographers say. «إذا» is for the future and «إذ» for the past. As for the statement of Abū ʿUbayd that he chooses «إذا دبر» because after it comes وَالصُّبْحِ إِذا أَسْفَرَ — [this is not binding,] because Allah the Exalted swears by whatever He wills, and no judgement may be imposed on that requiring both to be future or both past.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: «[Translator's note: the source begins with «أن إن», apparently a corruption.]» "The Fire is one of the enormous matters." Abū Razīn said: «إنها», i.e. Jahannam. And الْكُبَرِ [is] with alif and lām; dropping them is not permissible according to any grammarian, and nothing of this [pattern] has come in the speech of the Arabs without alif and lām except أخر, and for that reason it was made a diptote.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
Al-Ḥasan said: there is no warner more calamitous than the Fire — or words to that effect. Abū Razīn said: Allah the Exalted says: "I am a warner to mankind". Ibn Zayd said: Muḥammad ﷺ is a warner to mankind. Abū Jaʿfar said: these are the views of the exegetes, and the closest [interpretations] can be derived from them. On the accusative of نذير there are seven views. It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «أنا» «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the pronoun in «إنها» is meant.]»; and it may be a ḥāl from إحدى الكبر. These two views are derived from the view of al-Ḥasan, because he made the Fire the one that warns. The construction may be: "and none knows the hosts of your Lord except He, as a warner to mankind"; and the construction may be: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it thus, a warner to mankind" — these two views are derived from the view of Abū Razīn. Al-Kisāʾī said: i.e. "Stand, as a warner" — and this goes back to the view of Ibn Zayd. And نذير may mean "warning" (إنذار), as He said:
«فكيف كان نذير»; the construction would then be: "and We have made the keepers of the Fire nothing but angels, as a warning". Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the construction may be "I mean, a warner". Abū Jaʿfar said: the tāʾ «[Translator's note: the source has «الياء» (yāʾ); the feminine tāʾ is evidently meant.]» was dropped from نذير, when it refers to the Fire, in the sense of attribution (nasab).

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: [لِمَنْ شاءَ is] a badal (substitute) with the lām repeated; and without the lām it would have been permissible.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: رَهِينَةٌ is construed according to the meaning; if it were according to the wording, it would be رهين.

nahhas-irab:39-41.t: [أَصْحابَ is] accusative as an exception. It is soundly reported from two of the Companions of the Prophet that by أصحاب اليمين here are meant the angels and the children. What indicates this is that after it comes يَتَساءَلُونَ عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ ما سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ, and this is the speech of those who have committed no sin. Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr reading: يَتَساءَلُونَ عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ يا فلان ما سلكك في سقر. This reading is by way of explanation (tafsīr), and its chain of transmission is sound.

nahhas-irab:42-44.t:
وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ: the nūn was dropped because of frequent use; if it were brought, it would be good outside the Quran. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the nūn resembled the nūn that is dropped in the jussive in our saying:
يقومان and يقومون. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab said: he is mistaken; if it were as he said, it would be dropped in our saying لم يصن زيد نفسه.

nahhas-irab:45-47.t: وَكُنَّا نَخُوضُ مَعَ الْخائِضِينَ: the kāf was given ḍamma to indicate that it is from a root with wāw, so فعل was transferred to فعل «[Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes the two patterns (fa‘ala → fa‘ula) has been lost in print.]». And likewise وَكُنَّا نُكَذِّبُ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ حَتَّى أَتانَا الْيَقِينُ, i.e. "until"; and «أن» is implied after «حتى».

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: I.e. the intercessors do not intercede for them; and by this He indicated that intercession benefits others than them.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: «[Translator's note: the beginning of the entry, naming the first reading (مُسْتَنْفَرَةٌ, with fatḥa on the fāʾ), has dropped out of the source.]» [This is] the reading of the people of Medina and al-Ḥasan; and the reading of Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and Abū ʿAmr is مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ; and both readings are reported from al-Kisāʾī. Abū Jaʿfar said: «مستنفرة» [with kasra] is clearer in this, i.e. frightened; and مستنفرة [with fatḥa] is problematic «[Translator's note: the source text does not mark which vowel is meant in either case; the bracketed vowels follow the sense of the argument.]», because استفعل is mostly used when one seeks the action, as you say استسقى, when he asks to be given drink; and donkeys do not seek this. But the justification of the reading is that استنفر is in the sense of نفر, so the meaning is "fleeing".

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: [قَسْوَرَةٍ is] فعولة «[Translator's note: so in the source.]» from القسر. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned what the exegetes said about it.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: أَنْ يُؤْتى صُحُفاً مُنَشَّرَةً: [مُنَشَّرَةً is] according to the feminine of the group; and it was put in the singular because it is greater in number.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: Only assimilation (idghām) is permissible, because the first is vowelless.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: «وما تذكرون» is the reading of Nāfiʿ, with a shift of address; and most people read وَما يَذْكُرُونَ, so that it refers back to what preceded. وما تشاؤون إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ: with the object omitted because the hearer knows it. هُوَ أَهْلُ التَّقْوى: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). وَأَهْلُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ: «أهل» was repeated for emphasis and magnification; and if it had not been repeated, it would have been permissible.

safi-cedvel:1-7.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها المدّثّر) is like يأيّها المزمّل [Note: In verse (1) of the previous surah.], (الفاء) conjunction ...
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «قم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أنذر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قم.
(الواو) conjunction in the five places, and likewise (الفاء) [Note: This fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) according to al-Fārisī, and according to others it is the answer of an implied (muqaddar) (أمّا), i.e. "and as for your Lord, magnify (Him)"..
Ibn Hishām rejected that in al-Mughnī, because it involves one omission after another.. since (أمّا) is a substitute for (مهما يكن من شيء), so when it is omitted from the speech it is not replaced by anything, and there is no indication of its omission.. So it is then a conjunction that conjoins the verb after it to an implied verb, namely قم, or تنبّه, or the like.], (ربّك) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being كبّر, and (ثيابك, الرجز) are the two objects of (طهّر, اهجر) respectively; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive (majzūm); (لربّك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اصبر). The clause «كبّر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied clause that is conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative, قم.. i.e. "arise, and magnify your Lord".
The clause «طهّر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to another implied clause, i.e. قم.
The clause «اهجر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to another implied clause, i.e. قم.
The clause «لا تمنن ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to one of the request clauses.
The clause «تستكثر ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of تمنن.
The clause «اصبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to another implied clause, i.e. قم.

* Morphology:
(1) المدّثّر: active participle of the five-letter verb تدثّر, i.e. he put on the دثار, which is the garment.. i.e. the one wrapped in his garments. In it the tāʾ of the pattern تفعّل has been changed into a dāl for assimilation; its pattern is متفعّل [Note: See verse (1) of Surat al-Muzzammil.].
(5) الرجز: with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and it is the same as الرجز with kasra on it.. see verse (59) of Surat al-Baqara.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ».
It was said: it is a metonymy for a command to purify the soul of deeds that are found filthy and states that are found repugnant. One says "So-and-so is clean of hem and sleeves" when they describe him as free of faults and of the stains of character.
The loose metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ».
The literal meaning of الرجز is severe punishment, and what is meant here is the worship of idols. So it was expressed by الرجز — which is severe punishment — because it is caused by the worship of idols; thus the relation of this figure is causation (al-musabbabiyya).

safi-cedvel:8-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (في الناقور) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, because it is annexed to an indeclinable word, in the position of an accusative — badal (substitute) of إذا [Note: Or a badal of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك), so it is in the position of a nominative.], and إذ is an adverbial noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn is the tanwīn of compensation; (يوم) khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ذلك), nominative; (على الكافرين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عسير) [Note: Or attached to an adjective of it, or attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun in عسير.]; (غير) a second naʿt (adjective).
The clause «نقر في الناقور ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ذلك ... يوم عسير» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(الناقور): a noun meaning الصور — which is the horn; its pattern is فاعول, from النقر, which is striking.
(عسير): a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral عسر, of the pattern-class فرح and the pattern-class كرم; its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:11-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (من) relative noun, in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the position of the yāʾ in (ذرني); (وحيدا) ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted returning pronoun, i.e. "the one whom I created alone"; (له) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being جعلت, and the second (له) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مهّدت); (تمهيدا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أزيد ...) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (يطمع), i.e. "in that I increase him" or "for that I increase him".
The clause «ذرني ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خلقت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «جعلت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خلقت.
The clause «مهّدت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خلقت.
The clause «يطمع ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause مهّدت.
The clause «أزيد ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(11) وحيدا: a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral وحد, of the pattern-class ضرب..
It also comes, irregularly, from the pattern-class وحد يحد, with ḍamma on the middle radical in the past and kasra in the imperfect; its pattern is فعيل.
(14) تمهيدا: the regular maṣdar of the four-letter verb (مهّد); its pattern is تفعيل, with fatḥa on the tāʾ.

* Benefits:
- Disbelief and obstinacy:
When Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم) up to His saying (المصير), the Prophet ﷺ stood in the mosque praying, while al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra was near him, listening to his recitation. When the Prophet ﷺ perceived that he was listening, he repeated the recitation of the verse. Al-Walīd went off until he came to the assembly of his people of Banū Makhzūm, and said: "By Allah, I have just heard from Muhammad speech that is not of the speech of humans, nor of the speech of the jinn.
