By Allah, it has a sweetness, and upon it is a grace; its top is fruitful and its bottom is abundant; it rises high and nothing rises above it." Then he went off to his home, and Quraysh said: "By Allah, al-Walīd has turned apostate, and all of Quraysh will surely turn apostate." Abū Jahl said: "I will take care of him for you." So he went off until he sat at al-Walīd's side, looking sad. Al-Walīd said to him: "Why do I see you sad, O son of my brother?" He said: "And what keeps me from being sad, when here are Quraysh collecting money for you to help you in your old age, and they claim that you have embellished Muhammad's speech, and that you go in to Ibn Abī Kabsha and Ibn Abī Quḥāfa to get some of their leftover food." Al-Walīd became angry and said: "Does Quraysh not know that I am among the richest of them in wealth and children? And have Muhammad and his companions ever had their fill of food, that they should have leftover food?" Then he got up with Abū Jahl until he came to the assembly of his people, and said to them: "You claim that Muhammad is mad; have you ever seen him rage?" They said: "By Allah, no." He said: "You claim that he is a soothsayer; have you ever seen him practise soothsaying?" They said: "By Allah, no." He said: "You claim that he is a poet; have you ever seen him utter poetry?" They said: "By Allah, no." He said: "You claim that he is a liar; have you ever found anything of lying in him?" They said: "By Allah, no." Then Quraysh said to al-Walīd: "So what is he?" He thought to himself, then said:
"He is nothing but a sorcerer. Have you not seen him separate a man from his family, his children and his clients? So he is a sorcerer, and what he says is sorcery handed down." That is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: «إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ. فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ. ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ. ثُمَّ نَظَرَ. ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ. ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ. فَقالَ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ». When he said that, the assembly shook with joy, and they dispersed marvelling at him.

safi-cedvel:16-25.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke; (لآياتنا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عنيدا), meaning (جاحدا) "denying"; (صعودا) tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «إنّه كان لآياتنا ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the deterrence.
The clause «كان لآياتنا ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of the (first) إنّ.
The clause «سأرهقه ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
(الواو) conjunction, and likewise (الفاء) and (ثمّ) in the four places; (كيف) interrogative noun, in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), its governor being قدّر.
The clause «إنّه فكّر ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «فكّر ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of the (second) إنّ.
The clause «قدّر ...» is in the position of a nominative: conjoined to the clause فكّر.
The clause «قتل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّه فكّر.
The clause «قدّر ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «قتل (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قتل (the first).
The clause «قدّر (the second)» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption emphasizing the first.
The clause «نظر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the second clause قدّر [Note: Or conjoined to the first clause قدّر, so it is in the position of a nominative, and what lies between the two clauses is parenthetical.].
The clause «عبس ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نظر.
The clause «بسر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause عبس — or نظر —.
The clause «أدبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause عبس.
The clause «استكبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause عبس.
(الفاء) conjunction; (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (al-ḥaṣr); and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to سحر; (إن هذا إلّا قول) is like إن هذا إلّا سحر..
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause استكبر.
The clause «إن هذا إلّا سحر ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إن هذا إلّا قول ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «يؤثر ...» is in the position of a nominative: naʿt (adjective) of سحر.

* Morphology:
(صعودا): with fatḥa on the ṣād, a noun meaning the arduous mountain-path, or the hardship of punishment; its pattern is فعول, with fatḥa then ḍamma.

safi-cedvel:26-30.t:
* I'rab:
(سقر) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: Or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «في سقر», by making (أصليه) carry the meaning of أحرقه "I will burn him".], and it is denied tanwīn because of being a proper name and feminine.
The clause «سأصليه سقر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a badal (substitute) of (سأرهقه صعودا).].
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) interrogative noun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) in both places; (سقر) khabar (predicate) of the second.
The clause «ما أدراك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: It may be parenthetical between the ḥāl and its governor — or the one it describes —, and the parenthesis is for magnifying and making it awesome.].
The clause «أدراك ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
The clause «ما سقر ...» is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the object of the verb أدراك, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
(لا) negative; (الواو) conjunction; and the object of (تبقي) and (تذر) is omitted; (لوّاحة) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هي; (البشر) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi of the intensive form لوّاحة, and (اللام) is for strengthening (al-taqwiya); (عليها) attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (تسعة عشر) two numeral parts, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative as delayed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «لا تبقي ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the second سقر, the governor of it being the sense of magnification in His saying ما سقر.. or a ḥāl of the first سقر.
(3, 4) Or in the position of an accusative as ḥāl of the second or the first سقر].
The clause «لا تذر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لا تبقي.
The clause «(هي) لوّاحة ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption «3».
The clause «عليها تسعة عشر ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption «4».

* Morphology:
(29) (لوّاحة): feminine of لوّاح, an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) from لاح يلوح, meaning "it altered the skin", or meaning "it appeared" [Note: This meaning makes the (اللام) in His saying للبشر a preposition attached to (لوّاحة).]; and اللوح is also severe thirst.. Its pattern is فعّال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(البشر): plural of بشرة, meaning skin. A non-derived noun (ism jāmid); its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām, and the pattern of البشر is فعل, with two fatḥas.. And البشر may be a collective noun for people.

* Rhetoric:
The art of ambiguity (fann al-ibhām): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ». This art is that the speaker says something that bears two different meanings, neither of which is distinguished from the other. In this noble verse there are several possible meanings, among them: that the nature of this number, falling one short of the set of twenty, is such that whoever does not believe in Allah and His wisdom is put to trial by it, and objects and mocks, and does not submit as the believer submits, even if the wisdom behind it is hidden from him. It is as though it were said: We have made their number a number whose nature is to be a trial, for the sake of the believer's certainty and the disbeliever's bewilderment, and the certainty of the People of the Book, because their number is nineteen in the two Scriptures, so when they hear the like of it in the Qur'an they become certain that it is sent down from Allah; and the believers' increase in faith through their affirming that, just as they affirmed everything else that was sent down.

* Benefits:
- Omission of the tamyīz (specification):
The tamyīz is omitted when it is understood from the context of the speech, as in the verse we are dealing with (عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ), i.e. nineteen angels. And in our saying (كم صمت), i.e. how many days did you fast. And the saying of the Exalted: (إِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صابِرُونَ). It is irregular in the chapter of (نعم), as in «من توضأ يوم الجمعة فبها ونعمت», i.e. he has taken the concession, and an excellent concession it is.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative in the four places; (إلّا) for restriction (al-ḥaṣr) in the four places; (ملائكة) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and likewise (فتنة); (للذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (فتنة); (اللام) of reason (al-taʿlīl); (يستيقن) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; and (الواو) in (أوتوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in both places; (يزداد) imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يستيقن).. (إيمانا) tamyīz (specification).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يستيقن ...) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to the second (جعلنا).
(الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative; (يرتاب) imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يستيقن); (ليقول) is like ليستيقن; (في قلوبهم) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (مرض); (ماذا) interrogative noun, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أراد [Note: Or (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; (ذا) a relative noun, khabar; and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause أراد is the ṣila (relative clause) of ذا.]; (بهذا) attached to (أراد); (مثلا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the demonstrative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقول..) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to the second (جعل), so it is conjoined to the first maṣdar.
(كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its governor being يضلّ; (من) relative noun, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi in both places, of the two verbs of misguiding and guiding; (هو) detached pronoun, in the position of a nominative as fāʿil (agent) of (يعلم); (هي) detached pronoun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar being (ذكرى); (للبشر) attached to (ذكرى).
The clause «ما جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما جعلنا (the second) ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يستيقن ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يزداد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يستيقن.
The clause «لا يرتاب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يستيقن.
The clause «أوتوا.. (the second)» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يقول ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «في قلوبهم مرض ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the fifth relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أراد ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يضلّ الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the first relative noun (من).
The clause «يهدي ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يضلّ.
The clause «يشاء (the second) ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (من). The clause «ما يعلم ... إلّا هو» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يضلّ الله..
The clause «ما هي إلّا ذكرى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clauses يضلّ الله..

* Morphology:
(يرتاب): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is يرتيب: the yāʾ was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif, and the conversion carries over from the past tense ارتاب; its pattern is يفتعل.

* Benefits:
Preference (al-tarjīḥ):
Sometimes two valid analyses occur in i'rab, but we judge one of the two to be preferred on the basis of another usage that testifies to it in a parallel place. An example of that is what Makkī said about the saying of the Exalted: (ماذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِهذا مَثَلًا يُضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيراً): that the clause (يضلّ) is an adjective of (مثلا) or resumptive. The correct one is the second analysis, namely resumption, because of the saying of the Exalted in Surat al-Muddaththir, in the verse we are dealing with: (ماذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِهذا مَثَلًا؟ كَذلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ).

safi-cedvel:32-37.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke [Note: Al-Jalāl al-Maḥallī made it an opening particle meaning ألا, and al-Farrāʾ and some of the Basrans made it carry the meaning of the answering particle that precedes an oath, (إي), with kasra on the hamza.]; (الواو) the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (الليل, الصبح) conjoined to القمر, genitive; (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of an accusative, attached to the omitted verb of oath; (إذا) an adverb of future time, stripped of condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to the implied verb of oath; and the pronoun is the noun of (إنّ), referring to سقر; (اللام) for emphasis, in the place of the lām of oath, in compensation for the shifted lām (al-muzaḥlaqa); (إحدى) khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative..
The clause «(أقسم) بالقمر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أدبر ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أسفر ...» is in the position of a genitive, by (إذا) being annexed to it.
The clause «إنّها لإحدى ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the oath.
(نذيرا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of إحدى, its governor being the emphasis [Note: The word comes in the masculine because إحدى is made to carry the meaning of punishment.. It was said that it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in إحدى, its governor being the sense of magnification, i.e. "the greatest of the great things, as a warning".. It was said that it is a ḥāl of الكبر or of its pronoun..
They allowed it to be a tamyīz (specification), by making it a maṣdar meaning الإنذار "warning", like نكير meaning الإنكار.. or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, if it is a maṣdar..]; (للبشر) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نذيرا); (لمن) badal (substitute) of البشر, with repetition of the preposition; (منكم) attached to a ḥāl of the returning pronoun; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative; (أو) a conjunction.
The clause «شاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «يتقدّم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتقدّم) is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb شاء.
The clause «يتأخّر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يتقدّم.

* Morphology:
(35) الكبر: plural of كبري, feminine of أكبر; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then fatḥa. [Translator's note: the source prints كبري; the usual spelling is كبرى.]

safi-cedvel:38-42.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.]; (إلّا) for exception; (أصحاب) excepted by إلّا, accusative [Note: The exception is connected (muttaṣil), from كلّ نفس.. It was said it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), by interpreting the meaning as "every disbelieving soul is held for its deeds in the Fire".]..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كسبت) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رهينة), meaning مرهونة "pledged".
(في جنّات) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يتساءلون [Note: Or attached to an omitted khabar, its implied form being هم, and the clause is an explanatory resumption.]; (عن المجرمين) attached to (يتساءلون), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "about the state of the criminals"; (ما) interrogative noun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause سلككم; (في سقر) attached to (سلككم), i.e. "made you enter".
The clause «كلّ نفس.. رهينة» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كسبت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «يتساءلون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «ما سلككم ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech of an implied verb of saying, i.e.:
"They say after that: ما سلككم".. and the implied clause of saying is resumptive.
The clause «سلككم ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).

* Morphology:
(38) رهينة: feminine of رهين — see verse (21) of Surat al-Ṭūr — a derived adjective. It is better left without being interpreted in the sense of a passive participle — since فعيل in the sense of مفعول does not take the feminine tāʾ, but masculine and feminine are the same in it — and it may be a maṣdar used to mean the object, like الشتيمة — on the view of al-Zamakhsharī — who said: because Allah the Exalted made the obligation laid on His servants like a debt upon them, and their souls are pledged.

safi-cedvel:43-47.t:
* I'rab:
(نك) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the sukūn appearing on the nūn that is omitted for lightening; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن [Translator's note: the source prints تقديمه, evidently for تقديره "its implied form".]; (من المصلّين) attached to the khabar (predicate) of نك; (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نخوض).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لم نك ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لم نك (the second)» is in the position of an accusative: conjoined to the clause لم نك (the first).
The clause «نطعم ...» is in the position of an accusative: khabar of نك.
The clause «كنّا نخوض ...» is in the position of an accusative: conjoined to the clause لم نك (the first).
The clause «نخوض ...» is in the position of an accusative: khabar of كنّا.
(بيوم) attached to (نكذّب); (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أتانا ...) is in the position of a genitive by (حتّى), attached to the four actions: not praying, not feeding, plunging in vain talk, and denying..
The clause «كنّا نكذّب ...» is in the position of an accusative: conjoined to the clause that is the object of speech.
The clause «نكذّب ...» is in the position of an accusative: khabar of (the second) كنّا.
The clause «أتانا اليقين» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(الخائضين): plural of الخائض, active participle of the triliteral خاض; its pattern is فاعل. In it the weak middle radical is regularly changed into a hamza; its original form is خاوض: the wāw came after the quiescent alif of فاعل, so it was turned into a hamza..

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the answer of an implied condition; (ما) negative.
The clause «ما تنفعهم شفاعة ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if this is their state, then no intercession will benefit them"..

* Rhetoric:
The art of negating a thing by affirming it (nafy al-shayʾ bi-ījābih): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «فَما تَنْفَعُهُمْ شَفاعَةُ الشَّافِعِينَ».
This art is that the speaker affirms something in the outward sense of his speech, on condition that what is affirmed is borrowed, then negates something connected with it figuratively, while what is negated in reality lies in the inner sense of the speech.
So in this noble verse the meaning is not that someone intercedes for them but the intercession of those who intercede for them does not benefit them; rather the meaning is the negation of intercession, and so the benefit is negated, i.e. they have no intercession that might benefit them.

safi-cedvel:49-51.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) interrogative noun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (لهم) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); (عن التذكرة) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (معرضين), which is a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the pronoun in (لهم); (من قسورة) attached to (فرّت).
The clause «ما لهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كأنّهم حمر ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl of the pronoun in معرضين, so it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila).
The clause «فرّت ...» is in the position of a nominative: second naʿt (adjective) of حمر [Note: Or in the position of an accusative as ḥāl of حمر, because it is particularized by the adjective, with قد implied, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the time of Allah's will", attached to (يذكرون).] [Translator's note: the second half of this footnote ("with the omission of a muḍāf … attached to (يذكرون)") appears to belong to verse 56 (إلّا أن يشاء الله); it is translated as printed.].

* Morphology:
(50) مستنفرة: feminine of مستنفر, active participle of the six-letter verb استنفر; its pattern is مستفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(51) قسورة: a non-derived noun (ism jāmid) meaning the lion, or a collective noun meaning the band of archers, having no singular from its own root.. And among the Arabs everything large and strong is a قسورة; its pattern is فعللة, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The unqualified simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ».
He likened them, in their turning away from the Qur'an and from listening to the reminder and the admonition, to donkeys that have fled from their enclosure because of what frightened them. In likening them to donkeys there is evident blame and a clear disparagement of their state, as in the saying of the Exalted: «كَمَثَلِ الْحِمارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفاراً», and a testimony against them of dull-wittedness and little intelligence; and you see nothing like the bolting of wild asses and their running on and on when something alarms them.

safi-cedvel:52-53.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (منهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (كلّ امرئ); (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun.
The clause «يريد كلّ امرئ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يؤتى ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤتى ...) is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb يريد.
(كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke; (لا) negative.
The clause «لا يخافون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(يؤتى): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is يؤتي — with a vowelled yāʾ at its end preceded by a tāʾ with fatḥa —: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.
(منشّرة): feminine of منشّر, passive participle of the four-letter verb نشّر; its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:54-56.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction; (من) a conditional noun making the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يشاء الله) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يذكرون), i.e. "except by the will of Allah" [Note: Or it is in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time.].
The clause «إنّه تذكرة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «من شاء ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «شاء ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «ذكره ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يذكرون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يشاء الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «هو أهل ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(56) التقوى: it stands in for the interpreted maṣdar in the passive, i.e. "worthy that He be feared"..

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {المدثر}: The majority read it with shadda on the dāl and kasra on the thāʾ, an active participle from «تَدَثَّر». Its original is «المُتَدَثِّر», and it was assimilated, like «المُزَّمِّل». In Ubayy's codex it is «المُتَدثِّرُ», on the original form referred to. ʿIkrima read it with the dāl lightened, an active participle of «دَثَّر» (with shadda), with the object omitted, that is, "the one who wraps himself", as stated above regarding «المُزَمِّل». From him also is fatḥa on the thāʾ, as it is a passive participle. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From «دَثَّره». One says: «دُثِّرْتُ هذا الأمرَ» and «عُصِبَ بك», as he said regarding «المُزَمَّل»." End of quotation. The meaning of «تَدَثَّر» is that he put on the dithār, which is the garment above the shiʿār, the shiʿār being what is next to the body. In the hadith: "The Anṣār are the shiʿār and the people are the dithār." «سيفٌ داثِرٌ» is a sword long without polishing. From it the ruined dwelling is called «داثِر» because its landmarks are gone. «فلانٌ دَثْرُ المالِ» means he is good at managing wealth.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {قُمْ}: It is either from the familiar "standing", or from «قام» in the sense of beginning to do something, as in his saying:

4378 - فقام يَذُوْدُ الناسَ عنها بسَيْفِه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Gloss: He set about driving people away from her with his sword ... [rest omitted in the source].)

and the other's saying:

4379 - على ما قام يَشْتِمُني لَئيمٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Gloss: Over what, a base fellow has set about reviling me ... [rest omitted in the source].)

according to one of the two views. The other view is that «قام» is redundant. There is something to consider in taking it in the sense of beginning to do something, because it would then become one of the sisters of «عَسَى», and it would need a khabar that is an imperfect verb free of «أَنْ».

His saying: {فَأَنذِرْ}: Its object is omitted, that is, "warn your people of the punishment of Allah." The better view is that no object is implied for it, that is, "carry out the warning."

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ}: He put the object first, and likewise what follows, to signal exclusivity according to those who hold that, or for emphasis. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ربَّك» is singled out for glorification (takbīr)." Then he said: "The fāʾ entered with the sense of a condition, as though it were said: 'Whatever happens, do not leave off glorifying Him.'" I say: The discussion of a fāʾ like this has already been given at His saying {وَإِيَّايَ فارهبون} [al-Baqara: 40], at the beginning of al-Baqara. The Shaykh said: "It is close to what the grammarians implied in your saying «زيداً فاضْرِب»; they said its implied form is: 'Be alert, so strike Zayd.' The fāʾ is the response to the command. This command either contains the sense of a condition, or the condition is omitted, according to the disagreement about it among the grammarians."

semin-durr:5-5.t: Ḥafṣ read «والرُّجْزَ» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and the rest with kasra. It is said they are two dialects with one meaning. From Abū ʿUbayda: "The ḍamma is the more widespread of the two dialects and the more frequent." Mujāhid said: "With ḍamma it is the name of an idol," and this is also ascribed to al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī; "with kasra it is a name for punishment." If it is taken as punishment, a muḍāf must be omitted, that is, "shun the causes of punishment that lead to it," or the effect is put in the place of its cause, which is a common figurative usage.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ تَمْنُن}: The majority read it with the assimilation undone (unassimilated). Al-Ḥasan and Abū al-Sammāl read it with assimilation. It has already been mentioned that for the jussive and the pausal form of this kind both ways are permitted; its verification was given in al-Māʾida at {مَن يَرْتَدَّ مِنكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 54]. The well-known view is that it is from «المَنّ», which is reckoning a favour against the one given, because of what was given. It is also said that it means "do not weaken," from their saying «حبلٌ مَنينٌ», that is, a weak rope.

His saying: {تَسْتَكْثِرُ}: The majority read it in the nominative, and there are two analyses. The first: that it is in the position of ḥāl, that is, "do not give for favour, regarding what you gave as much." It is also said its meaning is: "so that you take more than you gave." The second: that it is with «أَنْ» omitted, meaning that the original is «ولا تَمْنُنْ أَنْ تستكثرَ», and when «أَنْ» was dropped the verb became nominative, like his saying:

4380 - ألا أيُّهذا الزَّاجري أَحْضُرُ الوغى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Gloss: O you who rebuke me, that I should attend the battle ... [rest omitted in the source].)

in one of the two transmissions. Al-Zamakhsharī said it, and did not state the grammatical position of «أَنْ» and what it governs. There are two views: the more evident, which is what he intends, is that it is in the position of accusative or genitive, according to the disagreement about it after omission of the preposition, which here is the lām of reason, its implied form being «ولا تَمْنُنْ لأَنْ تَسْتكْثِرَ». The second: that it is in the position of accusative only, as an object, that is, "do not become weak about seeking more good." Makkī said it, and you have already seen that «تَمْنُنْ» means «تَضْعُف», which is Mujāhid's view. However, the Shaykh said after al-Zamakhsharī's words: "The Quran may not be interpreted on this basis, because that is not permitted except in poetry, and we have an alternative to it with the meaning of the ḥāl being sound." I say: Makkī and others preceded him in this. Moreover, his statement "in poetry" is rejected; these Kufans permit that. Furthermore, al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read «تَسْتَكْثِرَ» in the accusative, and that is with «أَنْ» implied, as in their saying «مُرْهُ يَحْفِرَها». More eloquent than that is the explicit mention of «أنْ» in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «ولا تَمْنُنْ أَنْ تستكثرَ».

Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī ʿAbla also read «تستكثِرْ» in the jussive, and there are three analyses. The first: that it is a badal from the preceding verb, as in His saying {يَلْقَ أَثَاماً يُضَاعَفْ} [al-Furqān: 68-69], where «يُضاعَفْ» is a badal from «يَلْقَ», and as in his saying:

4381 - مَتى تَأْتِنا تُلْمِمْ بنا في ديارِنا ... تَجِدْ حَطَباً جَزْلاً وناراً تَأجَّجا
(Gloss: Whenever you come to us and visit us in our homes, you will find plentiful firewood and a blazing fire.)

and it would be from the «المَنّ» in His saying {لاَ تُبْطِلُواْ صَدَقَاتِكُم بالمن والأذى} [al-Baqara: 264]. The second: that «ثِرْوَ» is made to resemble «عَضُد», and so given sukūn for lightness. Al-Zamakhsharī said this, meaning that you take from «تَسْتكثر» as a whole and the word after it, namely the wāw, what makes it resemble «عَضُد». Do you not see that he said "that «ثِرْوَ» be made to resemble"? He took part of «تَسْتكثر», namely the thāʾ and the rāʾ, and the conjunction from His saying {ولربِّك فاصبِرْ}. This is as they said about the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

4382 - فاليومَ أشرَبْ غيرَ مُسْتَحْقِبٍ ... إثماً من الله ولا واغلِ
(Gloss: Today I drink, bearing no sin from Allah, and no unbidden intruder.)

with sukūn on «أَشْرَبْ»: they took from the two words (رَبْغ) like «عَضُد», and then gave it sukūn. It has already been mentioned in Sūrat Yūsuf, regarding Qunbul's reading {مَن يَتَّقِي} [Yūsuf: 90] with the yāʾ retained, that «مَنْ» is relative, and the objection was raised from the jussive «يَصْبِرْ»; it was answered that it was made to resemble (بِرُف), taking the bāʾ and the rāʾ from «يَصْبر» and the fāʾ from «فإنَّ», and this is like «تيْكَ» exactly. The third analysis: that the state of pausing is considered and connected speech is treated as pausal. Al-Zamakhsharī also said this, meaning that it is nominative and was given sukūn for lightness, or connected speech was treated like pausal speech. The Shaykh said: "These two may not be relied on while there exists something preferable to them, which is the badal." I say: The truth is more deserving of being followed; how can one turn to these two analyses when the badal is evident in meaning, soundness and craft?

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {وَلِرَبِّكَ فاصبر}: The fronting is as stated above, and what made it good is that it is the head of a verse-ending, matching what precedes it. For «لربِّك» there are two analyses. The first: that it is the lām of reason, that is, "for the sake of your Lord, be patient with the harm of the disbelievers, and in the worship of your Lord, and away from everything unfitting"; what one is patient with and what one is patient away from were left out because both are known. The better view is not to imply anything specific but something general. The second: that «اصْبِرْ» is given the sense of "submit to your Lord and hand over your affair to Him, being patient," as in His saying {فاصبر لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ} [al-Qalam: 48].

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {فَإِذَا نُقِرَ}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The fāʾ in His saying «فإذا نُقِرَ» is for causation, as though it were said: 'Be patient with their harm, for before them is a hard day on which they will meet [the consequence] of their harm, and you will meet on it the consequence of your patience with it.' The fāʾ in «فذلك» is for the apodosis." I say: He means that the fāʾ in «فذلك» is the apodosis for the condition in His saying «فإذا نُقِرَ». As for what governs «إذا», there are several analyses. The first: that it is attached to «أَنْذِرْ», that is, "warn them when the trumpet is sounded." Al-Ḥawfī said this. There is something to consider in it, because the fāʾ prevents that; and had he intended to explain the meaning it would have been easy, but he is in the position of explaining the grammatical analysis, not the meaning.

The second: that it is accusative by what is indicated by His saying {فَذَلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ}. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is «إذا» accusative by, and how is it sound for «يومئذٍ» to be an adverbial for «يومٌ عَسير»? I say: «إذا» is accusative by what the apodosis indicates, because the meaning is: when the trumpet is sounded, the matter becomes hard for the disbelievers. What allowed «يومئذٍ» to be an adverbial for «يومٌ عسيرٌ» is that the meaning is: that day of the sounding is the occurrence of a hard day, because the Day of Resurrection occurs and comes when the trumpet is sounded." End of quotation. It is not permissible for «عَسير» itself to govern it, because according to the Basrans an adjective does not govern what precedes its qualified noun. For that reason al-Zamakhsharī's statement was rejected, that «في أنفسِهم» is attached to «بَليغاً» in His saying in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ [verse 63] {وَقُل لَّهُمْ في أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَوْلاً بَلِيغاً}; the Kufans allow that, and its verification has been given.

The third: that it is accusative by what «فذلك» indicates, because it points to the sounding. Abū al-Baqāʾ said it. Then he said: "«يومئذٍ» is a badal from «إذا», «ذلك» is the mubtadaʾ and «يومٌ عسيرٌ» is the khabar, that is, the day was sounded." The fourth: that «إذا» is the mubtadaʾ and «فذلك» is its khabar, with the fāʾ redundant in it; this is the view of al-Akhfash.

As for «يومَئِذٍ», there are several analyses. The first: that it is a badal from «إذا», as already stated in the third analysis. The second: that it is an adverbial for «يومٌ عسيرٌ», as stated in the second analysis. The third: that it is an adverbial for «ذلك», because it points to the sounding. The fourth: that it is a badal from «فذلك», but it is indeclinable (mabnī) because of its annexation to something not firmly declinable. The fifth: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and «يومٌ عسيرٌ» is its khabar, the clause being the khabar of «فذلك».

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {عَلَى الكافرين}: There are five analyses. The first: that it is attached to «عسير». The second: that it is attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «عسير». The third: that it is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «عسير». The fourth: that it is attached to «يَسير», that is, "not easy for the disbelievers." Abū al-Baqāʾ said it, except that it involves putting the dependent of the muḍāf ilayhi before the muḍāf, which is forbidden; some have allowed that when the muḍāf is «غير» in the sense of negation, as in his saying:

4383 - إنَّ امرَأً خَصَّني عمْداً مَوَدَّتَه ... على التنائي لَعِنْدي غيرُ مَكْفورِ
(Gloss: The man who deliberately singled me out for his affection, despite our distance, is with me one not to be denied his due.)

The verification of this was given at the end of al-Fātiḥa at length, so consult it there. The fifth: that it is attached to what «غيرُ يسير» indicates, that is, "it is not easy for the disbelievers." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the benefit of His saying «غيرُ يسير» when «عَسير» makes it unnecessary? I say: when He said «على الكافرين», restricting the hardship to them, He said «غيرُ يسير» to signal that it will not be for them, as it will be for the believers, easy and light, so as to combine the threat to the disbelievers and the increase of their rage with good news for the believers and consolation to them. It is also possible that it means: hard, with no hope that it will return to being easy, as the easing of hard matters of this world is hoped for."

His saying: {نُقِرَ فِي الناقور}, that is, a sound was made. One says «نَقَرْتُ الرجلَ» when you make a sound for him with your tongue, which is by pressing your tongue against the hollow of your palate. And «نَقَرْتُ الرجلَ» when you single him out for an invitation, as if you clicked for him with your tongue, pointing to him; this invitation is called «النَّقَرى», and it is the opposite of the general invitation «الجَفَلَى». The poet said:

4384 - نحن في المَشْتاةِ نَدْعُو الجَفَلَى ... لا تَرَى الآدِبَ فينا يَنْتَقِرْ
(Gloss: In the winter we call everyone to the general feast; you will not see the host among us picking and choosing.)

And Imruʾ al-Qays said:

4385 - أنا ابنُ ماوِيَّةَ إذْ جَدَّ النُّقُرْ
(Gloss: I am the son of Māwiyya when the clamour grew serious.) He means «النَّقْرُ», that is, the sound. He also said:

4386 - أُخَفِّضُه بالنَّقْرِ لَمَّا عَلَوْتُه ... ويَرْفَعُ طَرْفاً غيرَ جافٍ غَضِيضٍ
(Gloss: I lower him with the clicking when I mounted him, and he lifts a gaze that is neither harsh nor lowered.)

«والنَّاقُور» is of the pattern fāʿūl from it, like «الجاسوس» from «التَجَسُّس», and it is the thing that is sounded. In the exegesis it is the horn (ṣūr) that the angel blows. «والنَّقْرُ» also means striking a hard thing. «والمِنْقارُ» is the iron tool with which one pecks. «نَقَرْتُ عنه» means I searched for news about him, by metaphor from that. «ونَقَرْتُه» means I found fault with him; from it comes the saying of a woman to her husband: "Pass me by the sons of Naẓar, and do not pass me by the daughters of Naqar." By the sons of Naẓar she meant men, because they look at her, and by the daughters of Naqar, women, because they find fault with her and probe into her affairs.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ}: It is like {والمكذبين} [al-Muzzammil: 11] in the two analyses given in the preceding sūra.

His saying: {وَحِيداً}: There are several analyses. The first: that it is a ḥāl from the yāʾ in «ذَرْني», that is, "leave me alone with him, and I will suffice you in taking vengeance on him." The second: that it is a ḥāl from the tāʾ in «خَلَقْتُ», that is, "I created him alone, none sharing with me in his creation, so I own him." The third: that it is a ḥāl from «مَنْ». The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun, that is, "I created him alone." The fifth: that it is accusative as censure (dhamm). «وحيد» was an epithet of al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra. The meaning of «وحيداً» is: humble and few. It is also said he used to claim that he was unique in his excellence and wealth. There is nothing in that which requires his claim to be true, since this is an epithet by which he became known, and a person may be given an epithet he does not possess; and if it is an epithet, its accusative as censure is determined.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {إِنَّهُ كان لآيَاتِنَا عَنِيداً}: It is resumptive (istiʾnāf), an answer to someone who asks: why does his wealth not increase? What is the matter with him that he was repelled from his greed for that? It was answered with His saying {إِنَّهُ كان لآيَتِنَا عَنِيداً}.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ}: It may be a resumptive clause giving the reason for His saying «سَأُرْهِقُه». It may also be a badal from {إِنَّهُ كان لآيَتِنَا عَنِيداً}.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ عَبَسَ}: One says «عَبَسَ يَعْبِسُ عَبْساً وعُبُوساً», that is, he frowned. «والعَبَسُ» is what dries on the tails of camels of dung and urine. Abū al-Najm said:

4387 - كأن في أَذْنابِهِنَّ الشُّوَّلِ ... مِنْ عَبَسِ الصَّيْفِ قُرونَ الأُيَّلِ
(Gloss: As though on the tails of the she-camels with dried milk, from the summer's caked dung, there were the horns of stags.)

His saying {وَبَسَر}: One says «بَسَرَ يَبْسُر بَسْراً وبُسُوراً» when he contracts what is between his eyes out of dislike for something, and his face turns dark from it. One says «وَجْهٌ باسِرٌ», that is, contracted and dark. He said:

4388 - صَبَحْنا تميماً غَداةَ الجِفارِ ... بشَهْباءَ مَلْمومَةٍ باسِرَةْ
(Gloss: We met Tamīm in the morning at al-Jifār with a grey, compact, grim-faced host.)

The people of Yemen say «بَسَرَ المَرْكَبُ» and «أَبْسَر» when it stopped. «وأَبْسَرْنا» means we came to a halt. Al-Rāghib said: "«البَسْرُ» is [Translator's note: the source repeats «البَسْرُ:» twice here] hastening after a thing before its time, as in «بَسَرَ الرجلُ الحاجةَ», he sought it at the wrong time, and «بَسَرَ الفَحْلُ الناقةَ», the stallion-camel covered the she-camel before her heat. «ماء بَسْرٌ» is water taken from its pool before it has settled; from it unripe dates are called «بُسْر». And His saying {ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ} means he displayed frowning before its time, and at the wrong moment. If it is asked: His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, {وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَاسِرَةٌ} [al-Qiyāma: 24] does not mean they do that before the time, and you have said that this is said of what is before its time; I say: that points to their state before they are brought to the Fire, and the word «البُسْر» was specified to signal that this, together with the distance that afflicts them, takes the course of affectation and of what is done before its time. His saying indicates this: {تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ} [al-Qiyāma: 25]." End of al-Rāghib's words.

Conjunctions of different kinds were used in these clauses, each with its suitability. As for what is conjoined with «ثُمَّ», it is because there is an interval between the actions, and secondly because between looking and frowning, and between frowning and turning away, there is a delay. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ثُمَّ نظر» is conjoined to «فَكَّر وقَدَّر», and the invocation is a parenthesis between them." I say: by the invocation he means His saying «فقُتِلَ». Then he said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of «ثم» entering upon the repetition of the invocation? I say: it indicates that the second repetition is more intense than the first, like the poet's saying:

4389 - ألا يا اسْلمي ثُمَّ اسْلمي ثُمَّت اسْلمي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Gloss: Ho, be safe, then be safe, then again be safe ... [rest omitted in the source].)

If you ask: what is the meaning of the intermediate «ثم» between the actions that follow it? I say: to indicate that he was slow in reflecting and took his time, and that there was delay and distance between the successive actions. If you ask: why did He say «فقال» with fāʾ after conjoining what precedes it with «ثم»? I say: because when the word occurred to his mind after his searching, he could not stop himself from uttering it without deliberation. If you ask: why did the conjunction not come between the two clauses? I say: because the other clause stands to the first in the position of emphasis to the emphasised."

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ}: This is a badal from His saying {سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً}. Al-Zamakhsharī said it. If what is meant by «الصَّعود» is hardship, the badal is clear; if what is meant is a rock in Hell, as has come in some exegeses, the badal is difficult, and it would bear some resemblance to badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute), because Hell comprises that rock.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {لاَ تُبْقِي}: There are two analyses. The first: that it is in the position of accusative as ḥāl, the governing element being the sense of magnification. Abū al-Baqāʾ said it, meaning that the interrogative in His saying «ما سَقَرُ؟» is for magnification, so the meaning is: consider Saqar great in this state. The object of «تُبْقي» and «تَذَرُ» is omitted, that is, "it does not spare what is cast into it, nor leave it, but destroys it." It is also said its implied form is "it does not spare those cast into it, and does not leave any extreme of punishment but that it reaches him with it." The second: that it is resumptive.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {لَوَّاحَةٌ}: The majority read it in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "it is scorching." This strengthens the resumptive status of «لا تُبْقي». Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī read it in the accusative as ḥāl, and there are three analyses. The first: that it is a ḥāl from «سقرُ», the governing element being the sense of magnification, as stated above. The second: that it is a ḥāl from «لا تُبْقي». The third: from «لا تذرُ». Al-Zamakhsharī made its accusative one of exclusive designation (ikhtiṣāṣ) to inspire dread, and the Shaykh made it a confirming ḥāl; he said: "because the Fire that neither spares nor leaves can only be one that changes the skins." «لَوَّاحَةٌ» is an intensive form, and it has two meanings. The first: from «لاح يَلُوح», that is, to appear, i.e., it is visible to mankind (al-bashar), that is, the people; al-Ḥasan and Ibn Kaysān held this. The second, which the majority of people hold: that it is from «لوَّحه», that is, changed and blackened it. The poet said:

4390 - وتعجَبُ هندٌ أَنْ رَأَتْنِيَ شاحباً ... تقول: لَشَيءٌ لوَّحَتْه السَّمائِمُ
(Gloss: Hind is amazed to see me pale, saying: surely something has scorched him, the hot winds.)

One says «لاحَه يَلُوْحه» when it changed his features, and it was recited:

4391 - تقول: ما لاحك يا مسافِرُ ... يا بنةَ عمِّي لاحَني الهواجِرُ
(Gloss: She says: what has altered you, traveller? O my cousin, the midday heats have altered me.)

It is also said that «اللَّوح» is intense thirst. One says «لاحَه العطشَ» and «لَوَّحَه», that is, changed him, and it was recited:

4392 - سَقَتْني على لَوْحٍ مِنْ الماءِ شَرْبَةً ... سَقاها به اللَّهُ الرِّهامَ الغَواديا
(Gloss: She gave me a drink of water when I was parched; may Allah water her with it with morning rains.)

«واللُّوْحُ» with ḍamma is the air between heaven and earth. «والبَشَرُ» is either the plural of «بَشَرَة», that is, "changing the skins," [or what is meant by it is mankind]. The lām in «للبَشَرِ» is a strengthening lām, like that in {لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ} [Yūsuf: 43]. The accusative reading of «لَوَّاحَةً» strengthens the view that «لا تُبْقي» is in the position of ḥāl.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {عَلَيْهَا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ}: This clause has two analyses, I mean as a ḥāl and as resumptive. There are anomalous readings of this phrase, and analyses that match them. Abū Jaʿfar and Ṭalḥa read «تسعَة عْشَر» with sukūn on the ʿayn of «عَشر», for lightness, because of the succession of five vowels of one kind; this is like the reading of {أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً} [Yūsuf: 4], which has already been discussed.

Anas and Ibn ʿAbbās read «تسعةُ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and «عَشَرَ» with fatḥa; this vowel is a vowel of indeclinability (binā'), and it must not be supposed to be a case ending, for if it were a case ending it would be placed on the last noun, since the two words take the place of a single word; it was turned to ḍamma only out of dislike of a succession of five vowels. From al-Mahdawī: "Whoever read «تسعةُ عَشَر» did so as if from interpenetration, as though he intended conjunction, so he left the compounding and raised the hāʾ of the feminine, then returned to indeclinability and gave sukūn." End of quotation. So he took the vowel as a case ending. By his saying "gave sukūn" he means gave sukūn to the rāʾ of «عشر», since that is how this reading is.

From Anas also is «تسعةُ أَعْشُرَ» with ḍamma on «تسعةُ», and «أَعْشُرَ» with a hamza with fatḥa, then a quiescent ʿayn, then a shīn with ḍamma. There are two analyses of it. Abū al-Faḍl said: "It is possible that he pluralised «العَشَرة» as «أَعْشُر» and then treated it like «تسعة عشر»." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the plural of «عَشير», like «يَمين» and «أَيْمُن»." From Anas also is «تسعةُ وَعْشُرَ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the ʿayn, ḍamma on the shīn, and a wāw with fatḥa in place of the hamza. Its analysis is like that of the one before it, except that he turned the hamza into wāw to be extra light; and the ḍamma, as above, is for indeclinability, not case ending. Al-Mahdawī reported that «تسعةُ وَعَشَرْ» was read; he said: "He brought it in the original form before compounding, conjoined «عشراً» to «تسعة», dropped the tanwīn because of frequent use, and gave sukūn to the rāʾ of «عشر» with the intention of pausing."

Sulaymān ibn Qatta read with ḍamma on the tāʾ, a hamza with fatḥa, a quiescent ʿayn, ḍamma on the shīn and a genitive rāʾ in «أَعْشُرٍ»; the ḍamma on this reading is a case-ending ḍamma, because he annexed the noun to what follows it and gave both the case ending of two annexed words. This is a dialect of some Arabs, who undo the compounding of numbers and decline both as an annexation, like the saying of the rajaz poet:

4393 - كُلِّفَ مِنْ عَنائِه وشِقْوَتِهْ ... بنتَ ثماني عَشْرَةٍ مِنْ حَجَّتِهْ
(Gloss: He was burdened, out of his toil and wretchedness, with a girl of eighteen years of his pilgrimages.)

Abū al-Faḍl said: "On this reading, which is the reading of whoever read «أَعْشُر», whether indeclinable or declined, because it is a plural, it is reported that the angels who are over Saqar are ninety angels." [Translator's note: the entry ends here in the source.]

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ فِتْنَةً}: It is a second object, with a muḍāf omitted, that is, "except a cause of trial (fitna)." «للذين» is an adjective of «فِتْنة», and «فتنةً» is not a mafʿūl lahu.

His saying: {لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ الذين}: It is attached to «جَعَلْنا», not to «فتنة». It is also said to be attached to an implied verb, that is, "We did that so that they may be certain." Al-Zamakhsharī has here a remark connected with the grammatical analysis, to draw it toward his aim of Muʿtazilism.

His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: It is an adjective of a maṣdar, or a ḥāl from it, as has been known many times. «ذلك» points to the earlier misguidance and guidance, that is, "just like that misguidance and guidance He misguides and guides." «مثلاً» is a tamyīz or a ḥāl. Calling this a "likeness" is by way of metaphor, because of its strangeness.

His saying: {جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ}: It is an object that must be placed first, because its agent is restricted, and because the pronoun refers back to what is attached to the object.

His saying: {وَمَا هِيَ}: The pronoun may refer to «سقر», that is, "Saqar is only a reminder." It may refer to the verses mentioned in it, or to the Fire because of its earlier mention, or to the soldiers, or the fire of this world, even though no mention of it occurred, or to the number. «للبشر» is the object of «ذِكْرى», and the lām in it is redundant.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {إِذْ أَدْبَرَ}: Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read «إذ», an adverbial for past time, with «أَدْبَرَ» on the pattern of «أَكْرَمَ». The rest read «إذا», an adverbial for future time, with «دَبَرَ» on the pattern of «ضَرَبَ»; the orthography allows both, so the written form does not differ. Abū ʿUbayd preferred the reading «إذا», saying: because after it comes «إذا أَسْفَرَ». He said: "And so it is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh." I say: He means that it is written with two alifs after the dhāl, one the alif of «إذا» and the other the hamza of «أَدْبَرَ». Ibn ʿAbbās also preferred «إذا», and it is related that when he heard «أَدْبَرَ» he said: "It is only the back of the camel that is 'udbira' (galled)."

They differed on whether «دَبَر» and «أَدْبَر» mean the same or not. It is said they have one meaning: one says «دَبَر الليلُ والنهارُ» and «أَدْبَرَ», and «قَبَلَ» and «أَقْبل». From it comes their saying «أمسٌ الدابرُ», which is from «دَبَرَ», and «أمسٌ المُدْبر». He said:

4394 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . ذهبوا كأمس الدابِر
(Gloss: [first hemistich missing in the source] ... they have gone like yesterday that has passed.)

As for «أَدْبَرَ الراكبُ» and «أَقْبل», they are only quadriliteral. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj. Yūnus said: "«دَبَرَ» means it ended, and «أَدْبَرَ» means it turned away," so he distinguished between them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«دَبَرَ» has the meaning of «أَدْبَرَ», as «قَبَل» has the meaning of «أَقْبَلَ». It is said that from it comes «صاروا كأمسٍ الدابرِ»; and it is said it is from «دَبَرَ الليلُ النهارَ» when it succeeded it."

The majority read «أسْفَرَ» with alif, while ʿĪsā ibn al-Faḍl and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «سَفَرَ» as a triliteral. The meaning: it threw the darkness off its face, by way of metaphor.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {إِنَّهَا}: that is, "the Fire." It is also said: "the coming of the Hour." The Shaykh related it so, and there are two difficulties in it: the pronoun's returning to something not mentioned, and the muḍāf's acquiring feminine gender. It is also said: the warning (nidhāra). It is also said it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa). The majority read «لإِحْدى» with a hamza with fatḥa, and its origin is a wāw, from «الوَحْدَة». Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim and Ibn Muḥayṣin, and it is also related from Ibn Kathīr, read «لَحْدَى» with the hamza dropped; this is so anomalous that it cannot be taken as a measure. Its analysis: that he turned it into alif, and then dropped the alif because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the rule for lightening a hamza like this is between it and the alif. The meaning of «إحْدَى الكُبَرِ» is: one of the calamities. He said:

4395 - يا بنَ المُعَلَّى نَزَلَتْ إحدى الكُبَرْ ... داهيةُ الدهرِ وصَمَّاءُ الغِيَرْ
(Gloss: O son of al-Muʿallā, one of the great calamities has befallen: the disaster of time and the deaf, blind changes of fortune.)

Likewise: "He is one of the men" and "she is one of the women," said of someone they regard as great. «الكُبَرُ» is the plural of «كُبْرى», like «الفُضَل», plural of «فُضْلى». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "the plural of «كبيرة»," and I think this was a slip on his part. There are two analyses of this clause. The first: that it is the answer to the oath in His saying «والقمرِ». The second: that it is a reason for «كَلاَّ», with the oath as a parenthetical for emphasis. Al-Zamakhsharī said it. I say: in that case an answer must be implied, which is forced and departs from the apparent sense.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {نَذِيراً}: There are several analyses. The first: that it is a tamyīz of «إحدى», since it contains the sense of magnification, as if it were said: "the greatest of the calamities in warning"; so «نذير» is in the sense of warning (indhār), like «النكير» in the sense of denial (inkār); similarly "she is one of the women in chastity." The second: that it is also a maṣdar in the sense of warning, but accusative by an implied verb. Al-Farrāʾ said it. The third: that it is of the pattern faʿīl in the sense of mufʿil, and a ḥāl from the pronoun in «إنَّها». Al-Zajjāj said it. The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «إحدى», as it is interpreted as meaning "the great". The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the agent of «قم» at the beginning of the sūra. The sixth: that it is a maṣdar accusative by «أَنْذِرْ» at the beginning of the sūra. The seventh: that it is a ḥāl from «الكُبَر». The eighth: a ḥāl from the pronoun of «الكُبَر». The ninth: a ḥāl from «لإِحدى». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it. The tenth: that it is accusative by an implied «أَعْني» (I mean). The eleventh: that it is accusative by an implied «ادْعُ», since what is meant by it is Allah the Exalted. The twelfth: that it is accusative by «نادِ» or «بَلِّغ», since what is meant by it is the Messenger ﷺ. The thirteenth: that it is accusative by what the sentence indicates, its implied form being: "You were great as a warner." The fourteenth: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «الكُبَرِ». The fifteenth: that it is a ḥāl from «هو» in His saying «وما يعلَمُ جنودَ ربِّك إلاَّ هو». The sixteenth: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, the governing element being the verbal sense in «الكُبَر». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "or «إنَّها لإِحدى الكُبر لإِنذارِ البشر»," and the apparent sense of this is that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; there is remoteness in it. If it is made a ḥāl from a feminine, it is not made feminine because it has the sense of "possessing warning," on the basis of relation (nasab). Abū Jaʿfar said its meaning.

The accusative is the reading of the majority, while Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read it in the nominative. If the Fire is meant, you have two analyses: that it is a khabar after a khabar, or that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "it is a warner"; the masculine is because of the above sense of relation. If what is meant is the Creator, the Exalted, or His Messenger, peace be upon him, it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "he is a warner." «وللبشر» is either an adjective, or an object of «نذير», with the lām redundant to strengthen the governing element.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {لِمَن شَآءَ}: There are two analyses. The first: that it is a badal from «للبشر» with repetition of the governing element, as in His saying {لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بالرحمن لِبُيُوتِهِمْ} [al-Zukhruf: 33] and {لِلَّذِينَ استضعفوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 75]; and that the object of «شاء» be put first, that is, "a warner to whoever wills to advance or to lag," and here the object of «شاء» is mentioned, though it has been said that it is not mentioned except when it contains something unusual. The second, to which al-Zamakhsharī inclined and with which he began: that «لمَنْ شاءَ» is a predicate put first and «أَنْ يتقدَّم» a mubtadaʾ put last. He said: "like your saying «لِمَنْ توضَّأَ أَنْ يُصَلِّي»; its meaning is: it is open to whoever wills to advance or lag, to advance or lag." End of quotation. His saying «التقدُّمَ والتأخُّرَ» is the implied object of «شاء», and his saying «أَنْ يتقدَّمَ» is the mubtadaʾ. The Shaykh said: "It is a meaning to which the mind does not readily go, and it involves omission."

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {رَهِينَةٌ}: There are several analyses. The first: that «رهينة» has the meaning of «رَهْن» (pledge), like «الشتيمة» in the sense of «الشَّتْم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not the feminine of «رهين» in the saying «كلُّ امرىء» because of the femininity of «النفس»; because if the adjective were intended it would be said «رِهين», since faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl is the same for masculine and feminine; rather it is a noun in the sense of «الرَّهْن», like «الشَّتيمة» in the sense of «الشَّتْم», as if it were said: every soul is a pledge for what it earned. From it is the verse in the Ḥamāsa:

4396 - أبعدَ الذي بالنّعْفِ نَعْفِ كُوَيْكِبٍ ... رَهينةٍ رَمْسٍ ذي تُرابٍ وجَنْدلِ
(Gloss: After the one on the slope, the slope of Kuwaykib, held as a pledge by a grave of earth and stones?)

as if he said: «رَهْنِ رَمْسٍ»." The second: that the hāʾ is for intensification. The third: that the feminine is for the sake of the word. The Shaykh preferred that it has the sense of mafʿūl and is like «النطيحة». He said: "What indicates that is: when it was a predicate of a masculine it was without hāʾ. Allah the Exalted said {كُلُّ امرىء بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهَينٌ} [al-Ṭūr: 21]. You see that where it was a predicate of a masculine it came without tāʾ, and where it was a predicate of a feminine it came with tāʾ. As for the one in the verse, it was made feminine in the sense of «النفس»."

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ أَصْحَابَ اليمين}: There are two analyses. The first: that it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), since what is meant by them is the sincere, righteous Muslims. The second: that it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), since what is meant by them is children or angels.

semin-durr:40-40.t: His saying: {فِي جَنَّاتٍ}: It may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are in gardens"; it may be a ḥāl from «أصحابَ اليمين»; and it may be a ḥāl from the agent of «يَتَساءلون». Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned these. It may also be an adverbial of «يتساءلون», which is more evident than its being a ḥāl from its agent. «يتساءلون» may be on its normal sense, that is, they ask others, like «دَعَوْتُه» and «تَداعيْتُه».

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ المصلين}: This is what indicates the agent of «سَلَكَنا» in such a way, occurring as an answer to the believers' saying to them: "What brought you into Saqar?" The implied form: "The lack of our prayer and such and such brought us in." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This clause takes the place of the agent, and it is the answer to «ما سَلَككم»," and what he means is what I have put forward, even though there is some difficulty in his wording.

Abū ʿAmr assimilated «سَلَككم», which is like {مَّنَاسِكَكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 200], and that has already been discussed in al-Baqara. His saying «ما سَلَكَكُم» may be with an implied "saying", and that saying would be in the position of ḥāl, that is, "they ask about them, saying to them: what brought you in?" Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how does His saying «ما سلككُمْ», which is the question to the criminals, correspond to His saying «يتساءَلون عن المجرمين», which is a question about them? That would correspond only if it were said: 'they question the criminals: what brought you in?' I say: His saying «ما سلككم» is not an explanation of the questioning about them; rather it is the report of the words of those who were asked about them, because those asked relate to the questioners what passed between them and the criminals, and say: we said to them, 'What brought you in?'"

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {فَمَا تَنفَعُهُمْ شَفَاعَةُ}: It is like his saying:

4397 - على لاحِبٍ لا يُهْتَدَى بمنارِه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Gloss: Upon a clear road whose signposts give no guidance ... [rest omitted in the source].)

in one of its two analyses, that is, "they have no intercession, so there is no benefit from it." It does not mean that there is an intercession that is not beneficial, as in His saying {وَلاَ يَشْفَعُونَ إِلاَّ لِمَنِ ارتضى} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 28].

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {مُعْرِضِينَ}: It is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition-and-noun phrase that occurs as khabar of the interrogative «ما». It has already been mentioned that a ḥāl like this is called an inseparable ḥāl (ḥāl lāzima), and a good discussion of it has already been given. «وعن التذكرة» is attached to it.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {كَأَنَّهُمْ}: This clause may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition-and-noun phrase, and be a badal from «مُعْرِضِيْنَ»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, meaning that it is as though it comprises it. It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُعْرِضِين», in which case it is a nested ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila).

The majority read «حُمُرٌ» with ḍamma on the mīm, and al-Aʿmash with sukūn. Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «مُسْتَنْفَرة» with fatḥa on the fāʾ, as a passive participle, that is, the hunters put them to flight. The rest read with kasra, in the sense of "fleeing": one says «استنفر» and «نَفَر» in the same sense, like «عَجِب» and «استعجب», «سخِر» and «اسْتَسْخر». The poet said:

4398 - أَمْسِكْ حِمارَكَ إنَّه مُسْتَنْفِرُ ... في إثْرِ أَحْمِرَةٍ عَمَدْنَ لغُرَّبِ
(Gloss: Hold back your donkey, for he is bolting after she-asses that have set off for the west.)

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though it seeks flight from its own selves in gathering for it and urging itself to it." End of quotation. So he kept the sīn in its usual sense of seeking, which is a good meaning.

Some preferred the kasra because of His saying «فَرَّتْ», for the sake of consistency. Muḥammad ibn Sallām related: "I asked Abū Sawwār al-Ghanawī, who was a pure-spoken Arab, and said: 'As if they were asses, what?' He said: 'Mustanfara (put to flight), a lion has chased them.' I said: 'It is {فَرَّتْ مِن قَسْوَرَةٍ}.' He said: 'Did they flee?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then mustanfira.'" End of quotation. He means that with «طَرَدها» it suits the fatḥa, because it is a passive participle, and when told that the recitation is {فَرَّتْ مِن قسْورة} he went back to the kasra for consistency. But a mutawātir reading is not rejected on the basis of an anecdote like this.

«القَسْوَرَةُ»: it is said to be the hunter. It is said to be the darkness of night. It is said to be the lion, and from it is the poet's saying:

4399 - مُضَمَّرٌ تَحْذَرُه الأبطالُ ... كأنه القَسْوَرَةُ الرِّئْبالُ
(Gloss: Lean and lithe, feared by the heroes, as though he were the qaswara, the lion.)

that is, the lion; but Ibn ʿAbbās denied it and said: "I do not know qaswara as the lion in the language of the Arabs; qaswara is only the band of men," and he recited:

4400 - يا بنتُ، كثوني خَيْرَةً لخَيِّرَهْ ... أخوالُها الجِنُّ وأهلُ القَسْوَرَهْ
(Gloss: O girl, be a good one for a good one, whose maternal uncles are the jinn and the people of the qaswara.)

It is also said that they are the archers, and they recited from Labīd ibn Rabīʿa:

4401 - إذا ما هَتَفْنا هَتْفَةً في نَدِيِّنا ... أتانا الرجالُ العانِدون القساوِرُ
(Gloss: Whenever we cry out in our assembly, there come to us the resolute men, the qasāwir.)

The clause of His saying «فَرَّتْ» may be an adjective of «حُمُر» like «مُسْتَنْفرة», and may be a ḥāl; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it.

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {مُّنَشَّرَةً}: The majority read it with shadda, from «نَشَّره» with doubling. Ibn Jubayr read «مُنْشَرَة» lightened. «نَشَر» and «أَنْشَرَ» are like «نَزَل» and «أَنْزَل». The majority also read «صُحُف» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, and Ibn Jubayr with sukūn. The Shaykh said: "What is preserved regarding a page and a garment is «نَشَرَ», lightened, triliteral." I say: this is refuted by the mutawātir Quran. Abū al-Baqāʾ said about Ibn Jubayr's reading: "It is from «أَنْشَرْتُ»: either in the sense of ordering that they be spread out, like «أَلْحَمْتُك عِرْضَ فلانٍ», or in the sense of «مَنْشورة», like «أَحْمَدْتُ الرجلَ», or in the sense of «أَنْشَر اللَّهُ الميِّتَ», that is, He gave him life, as if he gave life to what is in them by mentioning it."

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ}: Nāfiʿ read it with the second person, which is a shift (iltifāt) from the third to the second person; the rest read with the third person, following what precedes it in His saying {كُلُّ امرىء مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Muddaththir: 52], and they did not prefer the shift. The hāʾ in «إنَّه» refers to the Quran or to the threat.

His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ}: It has the sense of "except at the time of His willing", not in the sense that «أنْ» stands in for time, but with an omitted muḍāf.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t: Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ (١)). (الْمُدَّثِّرُ) is like «الْمُزَّمِّل», and it has already been discussed.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (تَسْتَكْثِرُ): in the nominative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); in the jussive as an apodosis (jawāb), or as a badal (substitute); and in the accusative on the implied form «لِتَسْتَكْثِرَ» (in order to gain more). The implied form, when it is made an apodosis, is: if you do not count your deed or your gift as a favour, you will gain more reward, because it is kept safe from being voided by reminders of favour, as the Exalted said: (لَا تُبْطِلُوا صَدَقَاتِكُمْ بِالْمَنِّ وَالْأَذَى).

ukberi-tibyan:8-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ (٨) فَذَلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ (٩) عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ (١٠)).
The words of the Exalted (فَإِذَا نُقِرَ): «إِذَا» is an adverb (ẓarf), and there are three views on what governs it:
First: it is what «فَذَلِكَ» indicates, because it points to the blowing; «يَوْمَئِذٍ» is a badal (substitute) for «إِذَا»; «ذَلِكَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is «يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ», i.e. the blowing of a day. Second: what governs it is what «عَسِيرٌ» indicates, i.e. difficulty; «عَسِيرٌ» itself does not govern it, because an adjective does not govern what precedes it. Third: it is explained according to the view of al-Akhfash, namely that «إِذَا» is a mubtadaʾ, its khabar is «فَذَلِكَ», and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). As for «يَوْمَئِذٍ», it is an adverb for «ذَلِكَ».
It is also said that it is in the nominative position as a badal for «ذَلِكَ»; or it is a mubtadaʾ, «يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ» is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «ذَلِكَ».
(عَلَى) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «عَسِيرٍ», or it is a naʿt (adjective) of it, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in it, or it is attached to «يَسِيرٍ» or to what it indicates.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَرْنِي وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وَحِيدًا (١١)).
The words of the Exalted (وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ): it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), or maʿṭūf (conjoined).
(وَحِيدًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the tāʾ in «خَلَقْتُ», or from the omitted hāʾ, or from «مَنْ», or from the yāʾ in «ذَرْنِي».

ukberi-tibyan:28-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا تُبْقِي وَلَا تَذَرُ (٢٨) لَوَّاحَةٌ لِلْبَشَرِ (٢٩)).
The words of the Exalted (لَا تُبْقِي): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سَقَرُ», the governor in it being the meaning of magnification [in «وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سَقَرُ»]; or it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), i.e. «هِيَ لَا تُبْقِي» (it leaves nothing).
(لَوَّاحَةٌ) in the nominative, i.e. «هِيَ لَوَّاحَةٌ» (it scorches); and in the accusative like «لَا تُبْقِي», or as a ḥāl from the pronoun in whichever of the two verbs you wish.

ukberi-tibyan:31-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا جَعَلْنَا أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَائِكَةً وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ وَيَزْدَادَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِيمَانًا وَلَا يَرْتَابَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَلِيَقُولَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ وَالْكَافِرُونَ مَاذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا مَثَلًا كَذَلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَمَا هِيَ إِلَّا ذِكْرَى لِلْبَشَرِ (٣١) كَلَّا وَالْقَمَرِ (٣٢) وَاللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ (٣٣)).
The words of the Exalted (جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ): it is an object that must be placed first, so that the pronoun [«هُوَ»] refers back to something already mentioned.
(أَدْبَرَ) and «دَبَرَ» are two dialectal forms. It is read both «إِذْ» and «إِذَا».

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (نَذِيرًا لِلْبَشَرِ (٣٦)).
The words of the Exalted (نَذِيرًا): there are several views on its accusative.
First: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in «قُمْ» at the beginning of the sūra. Second: [it is a ḥāl] from the pronoun in «فَأَنْذِرْ» — a confirming ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida). Third: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «إِحْدَى». Fourth: it is a ḥāl from «إِحْدَى» itself. Fifth: it is a ḥāl from «الْكُبَرِ», or from the pronoun in it.
Sixth: it is a ḥāl from the noun of «إِنَّ». Seventh: «نَذِيرًا» has the sense of «إِنْذَار» (warning), i.e. «فَأَنْذِرْ إِنْذَارًا» (so warn with a warning), or «إِنَّهَا لَإِحْدَى الْكُبَرِ لِإِنْذَارِ الْبَشَرِ» (it is indeed one of the greatest [things], for warning mankind). Among these views are some we do not approve of, but we have reported them. The preferred view is that it is a ḥāl from what the clause indicates, its implied form being: «عَظُمَتْ عَلَيْهِ نَذِيرًا» (it is great [in that respect] as a warner).

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ (٣٧)).
The words of the Exalted (لِمَنْ شَاءَ): it is a badal (substitute) with repetition of the preposition.

ukberi-tibyan:39-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا أَصْحَابَ الْيَمِينِ (٣٩) فِي جَنَّاتٍ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ (٤٠)).
The words of the Exalted (فِي جَنَّاتٍ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أَصْحَابَ الْيَمِينِ», or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَتَسَاءَلُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:42-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ (٤٢) قَالُوا لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ (٤٣)).
The words of the Exalted (لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ): this clause stands in place of the fāʿil (agent), and it is the answer to «مَا سَلَكَكُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:49-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ (٤٩) كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ (٥٠) فَرَّتْ مِنْ قَسْوَرَةٍ (٥١)).
(مُعْرِضِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition phrase [«لَهُمْ»]. (كَأَنَّهُمْ) is a ḥāl which is a badal (substitute) for «مُعْرِضِينَ», or [a ḥāl] from the pronoun in it.
(مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ) with kasra means fleeing, and with fatḥa means made to flee. (فَرَّتْ) is a ḥāl, with «قَدْ» implied with it, or another khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُؤْتَى صُحُفًا مُنَشَّرَةً (٥٢)).
(مُنَشَّرَةً) with doubling denotes multiplicity; and without doubling and with a sukūn on the nūn (مُنْشَرَة), from «أَنْشَرْتَ», either in the sense that he ordered it to be spread and enabled it, like «أَلْحَمْتُكَ عِرْضَ فُلَانٍ» (I gave you so-and-so's honour to feed on); or in the sense of «مَنْشُورَة» (spread), like «أَحْمَدْتُ الرَّجُلَ» (I found the man praiseworthy); or in the sense of «أَنْشَرَ اللَّهُ الْمَيِّتَ», i.e. He revived him — as though He revived what is in them by mentioning it.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ (٥٤)).
The hāʾ in «إِنَّهُ» refers to the Qurʾān, or to the threat.

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ. . . (٥٦)).
The words of the Exalted (إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ): i.e. except at the time of the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Muddaththir
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها المُدَّثِّرُ﴾ ("O you covered in a cloak"): the reading is with a doubled letter (tashdīd), the original being «المُتَدَثِّر»; the reason for it is like the reason in «المُتَزَمِّل», and its explanation is like the explanation of «المُزَّمِّل». It has also been narrated as «المُتَدَثِّر» with the tāʾ.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿ذَرْنِي ومَن خَلَقْتُ وحِيدًا﴾ ("Leave Me with the one I created alone"): we have explained the meaning of ﴿ذَرْنِي﴾ in [Sūrat] al-Muzzammil. ﴿وَحِيدًا﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is on two lines. One is that «وَحِيدًا» describes Allah, Mighty and Majestic; the meaning is: "Leave Me with the one I created by Myself alone; no one shared with Me in creating him." Or ﴿وَحِيدًا﴾ describes the one created, and the meaning is: "Leave Me with the one I created alone, having neither wealth nor child."

zajjaj:12-13.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مالا مَمْدُودًا﴾ ﴿وَبَنِينَ شُهُودًا﴾ ("And to whom I granted extensive wealth, and sons present [with him]"): its implied sense is "wealth not cut off from him"; and it was said: "a thousand dinars". «وَبَنِينَ شُهُودًا», i.e. present with him, not needing to go about [for a livelihood] and be absent from him. It was said that by this al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra is meant; he had ten sons and was wealthy.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُودًا﴾ ("I will burden him with an arduous ascent"), i.e. I will lay upon him a hardship of punishment.

zajjaj:18-19.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وقَدَّرَ﴾ ﴿فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾ ("Indeed, he thought and deliberated. So may he be destroyed how he deliberated!"): the meaning of «قُتِلَ» here is "may he be cursed", and similar to it is ﴿قُتِلَ الخَرّاصُونَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 10] ("Cursed be the liars").
Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra had said to the chiefs of the people of Mecca: "You have seen this man" — meaning the Prophet ﷺ — "and you know how his affair has spread. If people ask you about him, what will you say?" They said: "We shall say he is mad." He said: "Then they will speak with him and know that he is not mad." They said: "Then we shall say he is a poet." He said: "They are Arabs; they know poetry, and they know that what he has brought is not poetry." They said: "Then we shall say he is a soothsayer." He said: "Soothsayers do not say 'such-and-such will happen, if Allah wills', and he says 'if Allah wills'." So they said: "Al-Walīd has abandoned his religion (ṣabaʾa)." Abū Jahl, his brother's son, came and said: "The people are saying that you have abandoned your religion, and they have resolved to collect money for you as compensation for what you might be able to take from Muḥammad's companions." He said: "By Allah, they do not [even] eat their fill, so how could I take money from them, when I am among the wealthiest of people?" A group passed by him and mentioned to him what the Prophet ﷺ had brought, and he thought, and his face frowned and scowled (basara), i.e. he looked with intense displeasure, and he said: "This that Muḥammad has brought is nothing but magic he transmits from Musaylima and from the people of Babylon."

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿إنْ هَذا إلا قَوْلُ البَشَرِ﴾ ("This is not but the word of a human being"), i.e. this is nothing but the word of a human being.
